title.zh: 卷29 志第24 地理上
title.raw: 卷29 志第24 地理上 Volume 29 Treatises 24: Geography 1

sentences.zh: 序自古聖王之受命也，莫不體國經野，以為人極。

translations.literal: Preface: From antiquity, when sage kings received the Mandate, none failed to structure the state and regulate the fields, establishing the standard for humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Preface: From antiquity, when sage kings received the Mandate, none failed to structure the state and regulate the countryside, establishing the standard by which people should live.

sentences.zh: 上應躔次，下裂山河，分疆畫界，建都錫社。

translations.literal: Above they aligned with the celestial stations; below they divided mountains and rivers, demarcated borders, established capitals, and granted fief domains.
translations.idiomatic: Above they aligned with the celestial stations; below they divided mountains and rivers, drew borders, established capitals, and granted fief domains.

sentences.zh: 是以放勳禦曆，修職貢者九州；

translations.literal: Thus when Emperor Yao governed the calendar, the nine provinces maintained tribute and duties;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Emperor Yao governed the calendar, the nine provinces maintained their tribute and duties;

sentences.zh: 文命會同，執玉帛者萬國。

translations.literal: when Yu completed his work and assembled the lords, ten thousand states brought jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: when Yu completed his labors and assembled the lords, ten thousand states brought jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 洎乎殷遷夏鼎，周黜殷命，雖質文之用不同，損益之途或革，而封建之制，率由舊章。

translations.literal: When the Shang moved the Xia tripod and Zhou displaced Shang's Mandate, though the use of substance and ornament differed and paths of reduction and increase sometimes changed, the feudal enfeoffment system generally followed the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shang moved the Xia tripod and Zhou displaced the Shang Mandate, though the use of substance and ornament differed and the paths of reduction and increase sometimes changed, the feudal enfeoffment system generally followed the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 於是分土惟三，列爵惟五，千里以制畿甸，九服以別要荒。

translations.literal: Thereupon land was apportioned into three grades, ranks established in five levels; a thousand li defined the royal domain, and the nine concentric domains distinguished the inner from the outer and the wild marches.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon land was apportioned into three grades and ranks established in five levels; a thousand li defined the royal domain, and the nine concentric domains distinguished the inner regions from the outer and the wild marches.

sentences.zh: 十國為連，連有帥，倍連為卒，卒有正。

translations.literal: Ten states formed a lian; each lian had a leader; two lian formed a zu, and each zu had a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Ten states formed a lian, each with its leader; two lian formed a zu, each with its chief.

sentences.zh: 皆所以式固鴻基，蕃屏王室，興邦致化，康俗庇人者歟！

translations.literal: All these were means to solidify the great foundation, serve as a screen and barrier for the royal house, raise the state and bring about transformation, comfort the people and shelter them—were they not?
translations.idiomatic: All these were means to solidify the great foundation, shield the royal house, raise the state and bring about transformation, and comfort and shelter the people—were they not?

sentences.zh: 周德既衰，諸侯力政，干戈日用，戎馬生郊。

translations.literal: When Zhou virtue declined, feudal lords resorted to force; weapons were wielded daily, and war-horses were raised in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou virtue declined, the feudal lords resorted to force; weapons were wielded daily, and war-horses were raised in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 強陵弱，眾暴寡，魯滅于楚，鄭滅于韓，田氏篡齊，六卿分晉。

translations.literal: The strong oppressed the weak, the many tyrannized the few; Lu was destroyed by Chu, Zheng by Han; the Tian clan usurped Qi, and the Six Ministers divided Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The strong oppressed the weak and the many tyrannized the few; Lu was destroyed by Chu, Zheng by Han, the Tian clan usurped Qi, and the Six Ministers divided Jin.

sentences.zh: 其餘弑君亡國，不得守其社稷者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: The rest who regicides their lords, lost their states, and could not preserve their altars of soil and grain are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest who murdered their lords, lost their states, and could not preserve their altars of soil and grain, they are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 逮於七雄競逐，二帝爭強，疆埸之事，一彼一此。

translations.literal: When the seven powers competed in pursuit and the two emperors contended for supremacy, border affairs shifted back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the seven powers competed for dominance and the two emperors contended for supremacy, border affairs shifted back and forth.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇據百二之岩險，奮六世之餘烈，力爭天下，蠶食諸侯，在位二十餘年，遂乃削平宇內。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang held the strategic passes of the hundred-and-two, drew upon the accumulated strength of six generations, strove for the realm, and gradually consumed the feudal lords; after more than twenty years on the throne, he finally pacified the entire realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang held the strategic mountain passes, drew upon the accumulated strength of six generations, strove for the realm, and gradually consumed the feudal lords; after more than twenty years on the throne, he finally pacified the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 懲周氏之微弱，恃狙詐以為強，蔑棄經典，罷侯置守。

translations.literal: Taking warning from Zhou's weakness, he relied on cunning and deceit for strength, scorned and abandoned the classics, abolished feudal lords, and established commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Taking warning from Zhou's weakness, he relied on cunning and deceit for strength, scorned and abandoned the classics, abolished feudal lords, and established commandery governors.

sentences.zh: 子弟無立錐之地，功臣無尺土之賞，身沒而區宇幅裂，及子而社稷淪胥。

translations.literal: His sons and younger brothers had not even a pin's point of land; his meritorious ministers received not a foot of territory in reward; upon his death the realm split apart, and by his son's time the altars of state were lost.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger brothers had not even a pin's point of land; his meritorious ministers received not a foot of territory in reward; upon his death the realm split apart, and by his son's time the altars of state were lost.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖挺神武之宏圖，掃清禍亂，矯秦皇之失策，封建王侯，並跨州連邑，有逾古典，而郡縣之制，無改于秦。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han raised a grand vision of divine martial prowess, swept away calamity and disorder, corrected Qin Shihuang's mistaken policies, enfeoffed kings and marquises spanning multiple provinces and linked districts—exceeding the ancient norms—yet the commandery-and-county system remained unchanged from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han raised a grand vision of divine martial prowess, swept away calamity and disorder, corrected Qin Shihuang's mistaken policies, and enfeoffed kings and marquises spanning multiple provinces and linked districts—exceeding the ancient norms—yet the commandery-and-county system remained unchanged from Qin.

sentences.zh: 逮于孝武，務勤遠略，南兼百越，東定三韓。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu, he diligently pursued far-reaching strategy, annexed the Hundred Yue in the south, and pacified the Three Han in the east.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wu, he diligently pursued far-reaching strategy, annexed the Hundred Yue in the south, and pacified the Three Han in the east.

sentences.zh: 通邛、笮之險途，斷匈奴之右臂，雖聲教遠洎，而人亦勞止。

translations.literal: He opened the perilous routes to Qiong and Ze, severed the Xiongnu's right arm; though civilization's influence reached far, the people also grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the perilous routes to Qiong and Ze and severed the Xiongnu's right arm; though civilization's influence reached far, the people also grew weary.

sentences.zh: 昭、宣之後，罷戰務農，戶口既其滋多，郡縣亦有增置。

translations.literal: After the reigns of Emperors Zhao and Xuan, warfare ceased and agriculture was emphasized; the population grew ever more numerous, and commanderies and counties were also added.
translations.idiomatic: After the reigns of Emperors Zhao and Xuan, warfare ceased and agriculture was emphasized; the population grew ever more numerous, and commanderies and counties were also added.

sentences.zh: 至於平帝，郡國一百有三，戶一千二百二十三萬。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Ping, there were one hundred and three commanderies and kingdoms, with twelve million two hundred and thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Ping, there were one hundred and three commanderies and kingdoms, with twelve million two hundred and thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，承王莽之餘弊，兵戈不戢，饑疫薦臻，率土遺黎，十才一二，乃並省郡縣，四百餘所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the Han, inheriting the remaining evils of Wang Mang, weapons were not stilled and famine and pestilence came in succession; of the surviving people throughout the realm, only one or two in ten remained, so he merged and abolished more than four hundred commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the Han, inheriting the remaining evils of Wang Mang, weapons were not stilled and famine and pestilence came in succession; of the surviving people throughout the realm, only one or two in ten remained, so he merged and abolished more than four hundred commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 明、章之後，漸至滋繁，郡縣之數，有加曩日。

translations.literal: After the reigns of Emperors Ming and Zhang, the population gradually increased again, and the number of commanderies and counties exceeded that of former days.
translations.idiomatic: After the reigns of Emperors Ming and Zhang, the population gradually increased again, and the number of commanderies and counties exceeded that of former days.

sentences.zh: 逮炎靈數盡，三國爭強，兵革屢興，戶口減半。

translations.literal: When the Han line reached its end, the Three Kingdoms contended for supremacy; weapons and armor were raised repeatedly, and the population was halved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han line reached its end, the Three Kingdoms contended for supremacy; weapons and armor were raised repeatedly, and the population was halved.

sentences.zh: 有晉太康之後，文軌方同，大抵編戶二百六十余萬。

translations.literal: After the Taikang era of Jin, when writing and cart-tracks were unified, registered households totaled roughly two million six hundred thousand and more.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taikang era of Jin, when writing and cart-tracks were unified, registered households totaled roughly two million six hundred thousand and more.

sentences.zh: 尋而五胡逆亂，二帝播遷，東晉洎于宋、齊，僻陋江左，苻、姚之與劉、石，竊據中原，事蹟糾紛，難可具紀。

translations.literal: Soon the Five Hu rose in rebellion and disorder, the two emperors were driven into exile, and Eastern Jin down through Song and Qi occupied the cramped Jiangzuo, while Fu and Yao together with Liu and Shi usurped the Central Plains; the events and traces were tangled and confused, and cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Five Hu rose in rebellion and disorder, the two emperors were driven into exile, and Eastern Jin down through Song and Qi occupied the cramped Jiangzuo, while Fu and Yao together with Liu and Shi usurped the Central Plains; the events and traces were tangled and confused, and cannot be fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝除暴寧亂，奄有舊吳，，有州二十三，郡三百五十，縣千二十二。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang suppressed violence and pacified disorder, took possession of old Wu territory, and had twenty-three provinces, three hundred and fifty commanderies, and one thousand and twenty-two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang suppressed violence and pacified disorder, took possession of old Wu territory, and had twenty-three provinces, three hundred and fifty commanderies, and one thousand and twenty-two counties.

sentences.zh: 其後務恢境宇，頻事經略，開拓閩、越，克復淮浦，平俚洞，破䍧柯，又以舊州遐闊，多有析置。

translations.literal: Thereafter he strove to expand the territory and frequently undertook military campaigns, opening Min and Yue, recovering the Huai River coast, pacifying the Li caves, breaking Zangke, and because the old provinces were vast, many were subdivided.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he strove to expand the territory and frequently undertook military campaigns, opening Min and Yue, recovering the Huai River coast, pacifying the Li caves, breaking Zangke, and because the old provinces were vast, many were subdivided.

sentences.zh: 大同年中，州一百七，郡縣亦稱於此。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, there were one hundred and seven provinces, and commanderies and counties numbered accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era, there were one hundred and seven provinces, and commanderies and counties numbered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 既而侯景構禍，台城淪陷，墳籍散逸，注記無遺，郡縣戶口，不能詳究。

translations.literal: Then Hou Jing brought calamity, the capital fell, archives were scattered and lost, and records left nothing behind; commanderies, counties, and households could not be investigated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hou Jing brought calamity, the capital fell, archives were scattered and lost, and no records survived; commanderies, counties, and households could not be investigated in detail.

sentences.zh: 逮于陳氏，土宇彌蹙，西亡蜀、漢，北喪淮、肥，威力所加，不出荊、揚之域。

translations.literal: By the time of the Chen house, the territory shrank ever further: Shu and Han were lost in the west, Huai and Fei were lost in the north, and the reach of their power did not extend beyond the regions of Jing and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Chen house, the territory shrank ever further: Shu and Han were lost in the west, Huai and Fei were lost in the north, and the reach of their power did not extend beyond the regions of Jing and Yang.

sentences.zh: 州有四十二，郡唯一百九，縣四百三十八，戶六十萬。

translations.literal: There were forty-two provinces, only one hundred and nine commanderies, four hundred and thirty-eight counties, and six hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-two provinces, only one hundred and nine commanderies, four hundred and thirty-eight counties, and six hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後齊承魏末喪亂，與周人抗衡，雖開拓淮南，而郡縣僻小。

translations.literal: Later Qi inherited the disorders at the end of Wei and contended with the Zhou; though it opened up the Huai River south, its commanderies and counties were small and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi inherited the disorders at the end of Wei and contended with the Zhou; though it opened up the region south of the Huai River, its commanderies and counties were small and remote.

sentences.zh: 天保之末，總加並省，洎乎國滅，州九十有七，郡一百六十，縣三百六十五，戶三百三萬，周氏初有關中，百度草創，遂乃訓兵教戰，務谷勸農，南清江漢，西兼巴蜀，卒能以寡擊眾，戡定強鄰。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, all were merged and reduced; by the time the state perished, there were ninety-seven provinces, one hundred and sixty commanderies, three hundred and sixty-five counties, and three million three hundred thousand households. When the Zhou house first held Guanzhong, all institutions were newly established; they trained soldiers and taught warfare, promoted grain and encouraged agriculture, cleared the Jiang and Han in the south, and annexed Ba and Shu in the west; in the end they could use the few to strike the many and subdue powerful neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, all were merged and reduced; by the time the state perished, there were ninety-seven provinces, one hundred and sixty commanderies, three hundred and sixty-five counties, and three million three hundred thousand households. When the Zhou house first held Guanzhong, all institutions were newly established; they trained soldiers and taught warfare, promoted grain and encouraged agriculture, cleared the Jiang and Han in the south, and annexed Ba and Shu in the west; in the end they could use the few to strike the many and subdue powerful neighbors.

sentences.zh: 及于東夏削平，多有省廢，

translations.literal: When the eastern regions were pacified, many were abolished and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern regions were pacified, many were abolished and reduced.

sentences.zh: 通計州二百一十一，郡五百八，縣一千一百二十四。

translations.literal: In total there were two hundred and eleven provinces, five hundred and eight commanderies, and one thousand one hundred and twenty-four counties.
translations.idiomatic: In total there were two hundred and eleven provinces, five hundred and eight commanderies, and one thousand one hundred and twenty-four counties.

sentences.zh: 高祖受終，惟新朝政，，遂廢諸郡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, he renewed the government and abolished all commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, he renewed the government and abolished all commanderies.

sentences.zh: 洎於九載，廓定江表，尋以戶口滋多，析置州縣。

translations.literal: By the ninth year he had pacified the lands south of the Yangzi; soon, because the population had grown, he subdivided and established provinces and counties.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year he had pacified the lands south of the Yangzi; soon, because the population had grown, he subdivided and established provinces and counties.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，又平林邑，更置三州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he also pacified Linyi and established three additional provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he also pacified Linyi and established three additional provinces.

sentences.zh: 既而並省諸州，尋即改州為郡，乃置司隸刺史，分部巡察。

translations.literal: Thereafter he merged and reduced the provinces, soon changed provinces into commanderies, and established a Director of the Capital District to inspect and tour the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he merged and reduced the provinces, soon changed provinces into commanderies, and established a Director of the Capital District to inspect and tour the regions.

sentences.zh: 五年，平定吐谷渾，更置四郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, after pacifying Tuyuhun, four additional commanderies were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after pacifying Tuyuhun, four additional commanderies were established.

sentences.zh: 大凡郡一百九十，縣一千二百五十五，戶八百九十萬七千五百四十六，口四千六百一萬九千九百五十六。

translations.literal: In all there were one hundred and ninety commanderies, one thousand two hundred and fifty-five counties, eight million nine hundred and seven thousand five hundred and forty-six households, and forty-six million one hundred and ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and fifty-six persons.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were one hundred and ninety commanderies, one thousand two hundred and fifty-five counties, eight million nine hundred and seven thousand five hundred and forty-six households, and forty-six million one hundred and ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and fifty-six persons.

sentences.zh: 墾田五千五百八十五萬四千四十一頃。

translations.literal: Reclaimed fields totaled fifty-five million eight hundred and fifty-four thousand forty-one qing.
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimed fields totaled fifty-five million eight hundred and fifty-four thousand forty-one qing.

sentences.zh: 其邑居道路，山河溝洫，沙磧鹹鹵，丘陵阡陌，皆不預焉。

translations.literal: Settlements, roads, mountains, rivers, ditches and canals, sandy wastes, salty flats, hills, mounds, and field paths were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Settlements, roads, mountains, rivers, ditches and canals, sandy wastes, salty flats, hills, mounds, and field paths were not included.

sentences.zh: 東西九千三百里，南北萬四千八百一十五里，東南皆至於海，西至且末，北至五原，隋氏之盛，極於此也。

translations.literal: East to west it measured nine thousand three hundred li; north to south, fourteen thousand eight hundred and fifteen li; southeast reached the sea, west reached Qiemo, north reached Wuyuan—the Sui dynasty's greatness reached its peak here.
translations.idiomatic: East to west it measured nine thousand three hundred li; north to south, fourteen thousand eight hundred and fifteen li; southeast reached the sea, west reached Qiemo, north reached Wuyuan—the Sui dynasty's greatness reached its peak here.

sentences.zh: 雍州京兆郡京兆郡開皇三年，置雍州。

translations.literal: Yong Province, Jingzhao Commandery: Jingzhao Commandery—in the third year of Kaihuang, Yong Province was established.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province, Jingzhao Commandery: Jingzhao Commandery—in the third year of Kaihuang, Yong Province was established.

sentences.zh: 城東西十八裡一百一十五步，南北十五裡一百七十五步。

translations.literal: The city measured eighteen li one hundred and fifteen paces east to west, and fifteen li one hundred and seventy-five paces north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The city measured eighteen li one hundred and fifteen paces east to west, and fifteen li one hundred and seventy-five paces north to south.

sentences.zh: 東面通化、春明、延興三門，南面啟夏、明德、安化三門，西面延平、金光、開遠三門，北面光化一門。

translations.literal: On the east were three gates: Tonghua, Chunming, and Yanxing; on the south, three gates: Qixia, Mingde, and Anhua; on the west, three gates: Yanping, Jinguang, and Kaiyuan; on the north, one gate: Guanghua.
translations.idiomatic: On the east were three gates: Tonghua, Chunming, and Yanxing; on the south, three gates: Qixia, Mingde, and Anhua; on the west, three gates: Yanping, Jinguang, and Kaiyuan; on the north, one gate: Guanghua.

translations.literal: One hundred and sixty wards, two markets.
translations.idiomatic: There were one hundred and sixty wards and two markets.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，改州為郡，故名焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, Provinces were changed to commanderies, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye, Provinces were changed to commanderies, hence the name.

sentences.zh: 統縣二十二，戶三十萬八千四百九十九。

translations.literal: It governed twenty-two counties, with three hundred and eight thousand four hundred and ninety-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: It governed twenty-two counties, with three hundred and eight thousand four hundred and ninety-nine households.

sentences.zh: 大興開皇三年置。後周於舊郡置縣曰萬年。高祖龍潛，封號大興，故至是改焉。有長樂宮。有後魏杜城縣、西霸城縣、西魏山北縣，並後周廢。長安帶郡。有仙都、福陽、太平等宮。有關官。有舊長安城。始平故置扶風郡，開皇三年郡廢。武功後周置武功郡，建德中郡廢。有永豐渠、普濟渠。盩厔後周置周南郡及恆州，又有倉城、溫湯二縣，尋並廢。有司竹園，有宜壽、仙游、文山、鳳皇等宮。有關官。有太一山。有溫湯。醴泉後魏曰寧夷，西魏置寧夷郡。後周改為秦郡，後廢，又以新畤，甘泉二縣入焉。開皇十八年改縣名醴泉。有甘泉水、波水、浪水。有九抃山、溫秀嶺。上宜開皇十七年置，有舊莫西縣，十八年改名好畤，大業三年廢入焉。鄠有甘泉宮。有終南山。有澇水。藍田後周置藍田郡，尋廢郡，及白鹿、玉山二縣入焉。有關官。有滋水。新豐有溫湯。華原後魏置北雍州，西魏改為宜州，又置北地郡，尋改為通川郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢，及土門縣入焉。有沮水、頻山。宜君舊置宜郡，開皇初郡廢，有清水。同官鄭後魏置東雍州，並華山郡。西魏改曰華州。開皇初郡廢。大業初州廢。有少華山。渭南後魏置渭南郡，西魏分置靈源、中源二縣，後周郡及二縣並廢入焉。有步壽宮。萬年高陵後魏曰高陸，大業初改焉。三原後周置建忠郡，建德初郡廢。涇陽舊置咸陽縣，開皇初廢。有茂農渠。雲陽舊置，後周置雲陽郡，開皇初郡廢。有涇水、五龍水、甘水、走馬水。富平舊置北地郡，後周改曰中華郡，尋罷。有荊山。華陰有興德宮。有關宮。有京輔都尉。有白渠。有華山。馮翊郡後魏置華州，西魏改曰同州。

translations.literal: Daxing was established in Kaihuang year three. Later Zhou established a county on the site of the old commandery and called it Wannian. When Gaozu had not yet ascended, his enfeoffed title was Daxing, so at this point it was changed. It had Changle Palace. It had Northern Wei's Ducheng County and Xibacheng County and Western Wei's Shanbei County, all abolished by Later Zhou. Chang'an carried the commandery. It had such palaces as Xiandu, Fuyang, and Taiping. It had barrier offices and the old city of Chang'an. Shiping had formerly had Fufeng Commandery established there; in Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished. Wugong had Wugong Commandery established by Later Zhou; during Jiande the commandery was abolished. It had Yongfeng Canal and Puji Canal. Zhouzhi had Zhounan Commandery and Hengzhou established by Later Zhou; it also had Cangcheng and Wentang counties, soon both abolished. It had the Sizhu Garden and such palaces as Yishou, Xianyou, Wenshan, and Fenghuang. It had barrier offices, Taiyi Mountain, and warm springs. Liquan was called Ningyi by Northern Wei; Western Wei established Ningyi Commandery. Later Zhou changed it to Qin Commandery, then abolished it, and also merged Xinzhi and Ganquan counties into it. In Kaihuang year eighteen the county's name was changed to Liquan. It had Ganquan River, Bo River, and Lang River. It had Jiubian Mountain and Wenxiu Ridge. Shangyi was established in Kaihuang year seventeen. It had the old Moxi County, which in year eighteen was renamed Haozhi and in Daye year three was abolished into it. Hu had Ganquan Palace. It had Zhongnan Mountain and the Lao River. Lantian had Lantian Commandery established by Later Zhou; soon the commandery was abolished, and Bailu and Yushan counties were merged into it. It had barrier offices and the Zi River. Xinfeng had warm springs. Huayuan had Northern Yongzhou established by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed it to Yizhou and also established Beidi Commandery, soon changed to Tongchuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, with Tumen County merged into it. It had the Ju River and Pin Mountain. Yijun formerly had Yi Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Qingshui. Tongguan and Zheng had Eastern Yongzhou and Huashan Commandery established by Northern Wei. Western Wei changed it to Huazhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Shaohua Mountain. Weinan had Weinan Commandery established by Northern Wei; Western Wei separately established Lingyuan and Zhongyuan counties; Later Zhou abolished the commandery and both counties into it. It had Bushou Palace. Wannian and Gaoling: Gaoling was called Gaolu by Northern Wei and was changed at the beginning of Daye. Sanyuan had Jianzhong Commandery established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Jiande the commandery was abolished. Jingyang formerly had Xianyang County established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had Maonong Canal. Yunyang had long been established; Later Zhou established Yunyang Commandery, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had the Jing River, Wulong River, Gan River, and Zouma River. Fuping formerly had Beidi Commandery established there; Later Zhou changed it to Zhonghua Commandery, which was soon abolished. It had Jing Mountain. Huayin had Xingde Palace, barrier offices, the Jingfu commandant, Bai Canal, and Hua Mountain. Fengyi Commandery had Huazhou established by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed it to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 馮翊後魏曰華陰。西魏改為武鄉，置武鄉郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初改名馮翊，置馮翊郡。有沙苑。韓城開皇十八年置。有關官。有梁山，有鬼谷。郃陽朝邑後魏曰南五泉，西魏改焉。有長春宮。有關官，有朝阪。澄城後魏置澄城郡，後周並五泉縣入焉。開皇初郡廢。蒲城舊置南、北二白水。西魏改為蒲城，置白水郡，開皇初郡廢。下邽舊置延壽郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初並蓮勺縣入焉。有金氏陂。白水有五龍山、馬蘭山。扶風郡舊置岐州，統縣九，戶九萬二千二百二十三。雍後魏置秦平郡，西魏改為岐山郡，開皇三年郡廢。大業初置扶風郡。有岐陽宮。岐山後周曰三龍縣，開皇十六年改名焉。又有後魏周城縣，後周廢。有岐山。陳倉後魏曰宛川，西魏改曰陳倉。後周置顯州，尋州縣俱廢。開皇十八年置，曰陳倉。有陳倉山，有關官。虢後魏置武都郡，西魏改縣曰洛邑。後周置翔州，州尋廢郡開皇初廢，大業初改縣為虢。郿舊曰平陽縣，西魏改曰郿城，後周廢入周城縣，開皇十八年改周城為渭濱，大業二年改為郿。又後周置雲州，建德中廢。有安仁宮、鳳泉宮。有太白山、五丈原。普閏大業初置。有仁壽宮。有漆水、岐水、杜水。汧源西魏置隴東郡及汧陰縣，後改縣曰杜陽。後周又曰汧陰。開皇三年郡廢，五年縣改曰汧源。又有西魏東秦州，後改為隴州，大業三年州廢。有關官。有隴山、汧山、汧水。汧陽舊置汧陽郡，後周罷。南由後魏置，西魏改為鎮，後周復置縣。又有舊長蛇縣，開皇末廢。有關官。有盤龍山。安定郡舊置涇州。

translations.literal: Fengyi was called Huayin by Northern Wei. Western Wei changed it to Wuxiang and established Wuxiang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye the name was changed to Fengyi and Fengyi Commandery was established. It had Sha Garden. Hancheng was established in Kaihuang year eighteen. It had barrier offices. It had Liang Mountain and Guigu. Heyang and Chaoyi were called Southern Wuquan by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed them. It had Changchun Palace. It had barrier offices and Chaoban. Chengcheng had Chengcheng Commandery established by Northern Wei; Later Zhou merged Wuquan County into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Pucheng formerly had Southern and Northern Baishui established there. Western Wei changed it to Pucheng and established Baishui Commandery; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Xiagui formerly had Yanshou Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Lianshao County was merged into it. It had the Jinshi embankment. Baishui had Wulong Mountain and Malan Mountain. Fufeng Commandery formerly had Qizhou established, governing nine counties with ninety-two thousand two hundred and twenty-three households. Yong had Qinping Commandery established by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed it to Qishan Commandery, and in Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Fufeng Commandery was established. It had Qiyang Palace. Qishan was called Sanlong County by Later Zhou; in Kaihuang year sixteen its name was changed. It also had Northern Wei's Zhoucheng County, which Later Zhou abolished. It had Qishan Mountain. Chencang was called Wanchuan by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed it to Chencang. Later Zhou established Xianzhou, and soon both the province and county were abolished. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was established and called Chencang. It had Chencang Mountain and barrier offices. Guo had Wudu Commandery established by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed the county to Luoyi. Later Zhou established Xiangzhou; the province was soon abolished, the commandery was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang, and at the beginning of Daye the county was changed to Guo. Mei was formerly called Pingyang County; Western Wei changed it to Meicheng; Later Zhou abolished it into Zhoucheng County; in Kaihuang year eighteen Zhoucheng was changed to Weibin; in Daye year two it was changed to Mei. Later Zhou also established Yunzhou, which was abolished during Jiande. It had Anren Palace and Fengquan Palace. It had Taibai Mountain and Wuzhang Plain. Puyun was established at the beginning of Daye. It had Renshou Palace and the Qi, Qi, and Du rivers. Qianyuan had Longdong Commandery and Qianyin County established by Western Wei; later the county was changed to Duyang. Later Zhou again called it Qianyin. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished, and in year five the county was changed to Qianyuan. It also had Western Wei's Eastern Qinzhou, later changed to Longzhou; in Daye year three the province was abolished. It had barrier offices, Long Mountain, Qian Mountain, and the Qian River. Qianyang formerly had Qianyang Commandery established there, which Later Zhou abolished. Nanyou was established by Northern Wei; Western Wei changed it to a garrison, and Later Zhou restored the county. It also had the old Changshe County, abolished at the end of Kaihuang. It had barrier offices and Panlong Mountain. Anding Commandery formerly had Jingzhou established there.

sentences.zh: 安定帶郡。鶉觚舊置趙平郡。後周廢郡。並以宜祿縣入焉。大業初分置靈台縣，二年廢。陰盤後魏置平涼郡，開皇初郡廢。有盧水。朝那西魏置安武郡，及析置安武縣。開皇三年郡縣並廢入焉。良原大業初置。臨涇大業初置，初曰湫穀，尋改焉。華亭大業初置。有隴水、芮水。北地郡後魏置豳州，西魏改為寧州。

Liangyuan was established at the beginning of Daye. Linjing was established at the beginning of Daye, first called Qiugu and soon changed. Huating was established at the beginning of Daye. sentences.zh: 定安舊置趙興郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初置北地郡。羅川舊曰陽周，開皇中改焉。又西魏置顯州，後周廢。有橋山。彭原舊曰彭陽。後魏置西北地郡，有洛蟠城。西魏置蔚州，有豐城。西魏置雲州。後周二州並廢。開皇初郡廢，十八年改縣曰彭原。有珊瑚水。襄樂後魏置襄樂郡，後周廢。又西魏置燕州，後周廢。又有子午山。新平舊曰白土，西魏置豳州。開皇四年改縣為新平，大業初州廢。三水西魏置恆州，尋廢。上郡後魏置東秦州，後改為北華州。

Western Wei also established Xianzhou, which Later Zhou abolished. It had Qiao Mountain. Pengyuan was formerly called Pengyang. Northern Wei established Western Beidi Commandery there, and it had Luopan City. Western Wei established Weizhou, with Fengcheng. Western Wei established Yunzhou. Later Zhou abolished both provinces. Sanshui had Hengzhou established by Western Wei, soon abolished. Shang Commandery had Eastern Qinzhou established by Northern Wei, later changed to Northern Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 三水上郡上郡後魏置東秦州，後改為北華州。

sentences.zh: 統縣五，戶五萬三千四百八十九。

translations.literal: It governed five counties, with fifty-three thousand four hundred and eighty-nine households.

translations.literal: It governed eleven counties, with thirty-six thousand and eighteen households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eleven counties with thirty-six thousand and eighteen households.

sentences.zh: 上縣西魏置安寧郡，與安寧、綏德、安人三縣同置。開皇初郡廢，改安人為吉萬。大業初置雕陰郡，廢安寧、吉萬二縣入。又後周置義良縣，亦廢入焉。大斌西魏置，仍立安政郡。開皇初廢。有平水。延福西魏置，曰延陵。開皇中改焉。儒林後周置銀州，開皇三年改名焉。大業初州廢。真鄉西魏置。後周置真鄉郡，開皇初郡廢。開光舊置開光郡，開皇三年郡廢。有掞水。銀城後周置，曰石城，後改名焉。城平西魏置。開疆西魏置，有後魏撫寧郡，開皇三年郡廢。撫寧西魏置。綏德西魏置。延安郡後魏置東夏州。

translations.literal: Shang County had Anning Commandery established by Western Wei, together with Anning, Suide, and Anren counties. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Anren was changed to Jiwan. At the beginning of Daye, Diaoyin Commandery was established, and Anning and Jiwan counties were abolished into it. Later Zhou also established Yiliang County, which was likewise abolished into it. Dabin was established by Western Wei, which also established Anzheng Commandery. It was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had Pingshui. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Zhenxiang was established by Western Wei. Later Zhou established Zhenxiang Commandery, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Kaiguang formerly had Kaiguang Commandery established there; in Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished. It had the Yan River. Yincheng was established by Later Zhou as Shicheng, later renamed. Chengping was established by Western Wei. Kaijiang was established by Western Wei; it had Northern Wei's Funing Commandery, which was abolished in Kaihuang year three. Funing was established by Western Wei. Suide was established by Western Wei. Yan'an Commandery had Eastern Xiazhou established by Northern Wei.

translations.literal: The Western Wei changed it to Yanzhou and established a grand protectorate; in the Kaihuang era the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei renamed it Yanzhou and set up a grand protectorate, which was abolished during the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戶五萬三千九百三十九。

translations.literal: It governed eleven counties, with fifty-three thousand nine hundred and thirty-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eleven counties with fifty-three thousand nine hundred and thirty-nine households.

sentences.zh: 膚施大業三年置，及置延安郡，有豐林山。豐林後魏置，曰廣武，及遍城郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年改為豐林，大業初又並沃野縣入焉。魏平後魏置，並立朔方郡。後周廢郡，並朔方、政和二縣入焉。金明有冶官。有清水。臨真有西魏神水郡、真川縣，後周郡廢，大業初廢真川入焉。延川西魏置，曰文安，及置文安郡。開皇初郡廢，改縣為延川。延安西魏置，又置義鄉縣。大業中廢義鄉入焉。因城後魏置。後周廢，尋又置。義川西魏置汾州、義川郡，後改州為丹州。後周改縣為丹陽。開皇初郡廢，改縣曰義川，又廢樂川郡入。大業初州廢，又廢雲岩縣入焉。汾川舊曰安平，後周改曰汾川。大業初廢門山縣入焉。咸寧舊曰永寧，西魏改為太平。開皇中改為咸寧。弘化郡西魏置朔州，後周廢，開皇十六年，置慶州。

translations.literal: Fushi was established in Daye year three, together with Yan'an Commandery. It had Fenglin Mountain. Fenglin was established by Northern Wei as Guangwu, with Piancheng Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year eighteen it was changed to Fenglin, and at the beginning of Daye Woye County was also merged into it. Weiping was established by Northern Wei, which also established Shuofang Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and merged Shuofang and Zhenghe counties into it. Jinming had smelting offices and Qingshui. Linzhen had Western Wei's Shenshui Commandery and Zhenchuan County; Later Zhou abolished the commandery, and at the beginning of Daye Zhenchuan was abolished into it. Yanchuan was established by Western Wei as Wen'an, and Wen'an Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Yanchuan. Yan'an was established by Western Wei, which also established Yixiang County. During Daye, Yixiang was abolished into it. Yincheng was established by Northern Wei. Later Zhou abolished it, then soon established it again. Yichuan had Fenzhou and Yichuan Commandery established by Western Wei; later the province was changed to Danzhou. Later Zhou changed the county to Danyang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Yichuan, and Lechuan Commandery was also abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Yunyan County was also abolished into it. Fenchuan was formerly called Anping; Later Zhou changed it to Fenchuan. At the beginning of Daye Menshan County was abolished into it. Xianning was formerly called Yongning; Western Wei changed it to Taiping. During Kaihuang it was changed to Xianning. Honghua Commandery had Shuozhou established by Western Wei; Later Zhou abolished it, and in Kaihuang year sixteen Qingzhou was established.

sentences.zh: 合水開皇十六年置，大業初置弘化郡。馬嶺大業初置。華池仁壽初置。又西魏置蔚州，後周廢。歸德西魏置恆州，後周廢。有雕水。洛源大業初置。有博水、洱水。弘化開皇十八年置弘州，大業初州廢。弘德大業初置。平涼郡舊置原州，後周置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised five counties with twenty-seven thousand nine hundred and ninety-five households.

sentences.zh: 平高後魏置太平郡，後改為平高。開皇初郡廢。大業初置平涼郡。有關官。有笄頭山。百泉後魏置長城郡及黃石縣，西魏改黃石為長城。開皇初郡廢。大業初縣改為百泉。平涼後周置。有可藍山。會寧西魏置會州，後周廢，開皇十六年置縣。默亭。朔方郡後魏置夏州，後周置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Pinggao had Taiping Commandery established by Northern Wei and was later changed to Pinggao. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the county was changed to Baiquan. Pingliang was established by Later Zhou. It had Kelan Mountain. Huining had Huizhou established by Western Wei; Later Zhou abolished it, and in Kaihuang year sixteen the county was established. Moting. translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan. Lingwu Commandery: the Northern Wei established Lingzhou here; Later Zhou set up a grand protectorate, later abolished.

translations.literal: It governed six counties, with twelve thousand three hundred and thirty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised six counties with twelve thousand three hundred and thirty households.

sentences.zh: 回樂後周置，帶普樂郡。又西魏置臨河郡。開皇元年改臨河郡曰新昌，三年郡並廢。大業初置靈武郡。弘靜開皇十一年置。有賀蘭山。懷遠後周置，仍立懷遠郡。開皇三年郡廢。靈武後周置，曰建安，後又置歷城郡。開皇三年郡廢，十八年改建安為廣閏，仁壽元年改名焉。鳴沙後周置會州，尋廢，開皇十九年置環州及鳴沙縣。大業三年州廢。有關官。豐安開皇十年置。榆林郡開皇二十年，置勝州。

translations.literal: Huile was established by Later Zhou and carried Pule Commandery. Western Wei also established Linhe Commandery. In Kaihuang year one Linhe Commandery was changed to Xinchang, and in year three the commanderies were both abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Lingwu Commandery was established. Hongjing was established in Kaihuang year eleven. It had Helan Mountain. Huaiyuan was established by Later Zhou, and Huaiyuan Commandery was still established there. translations.literal: It governed three counties, with two thousand three hundred and thirty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with two thousand three hundred and thirty households.

sentences.zh: 榆林開皇七年置。大業初置郡。富昌開皇十年置。金河開皇三年置，曰陽壽，及置油雲縣，又置榆關總管。五年改置雲州總管。十八年改陽壽曰金河，二十年雲州移，二縣俱廢。仁壽二年又置金河縣，帶關。五原郡開皇五年置豐州，仁壽元年置總管府，大業元年府廢。

In year five it was changed to the Yunzhou grand administrative office. In year eighteen Yangshou was changed to Jinhe; in year twenty Yunzhou was moved, and both counties were abolished. In Renshou year two Jinhe County was again established, carrying the barrier. Wuyuan Commandery had Fengzhou established in Kaihuang year five; in Renshou year one a grand administrative office was established, and in Daye year one the office was abolished.

translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with two thousand three hundred and thirty households.

sentences.zh: 安化天水郡天水郡舊秦州。

sentences.zh: 上邽故曰上邽，帶天水郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初復置郡，縣改名焉。有濛水。冀城後周曰冀城縣，廢入黃瓜縣。大業初改曰冀城。有石鼓崖。清水後魏置，及置清水郡。開皇初郡廢。有關官。有分水嶺。秦嶺後魏置，曰伯陽縣。開皇中改焉。隴城舊曰略陽，置略陽郡。開皇二年郡廢，縣改曰河陽，六年改曰隴城。成紀舊廢，後周置。有龍馬城、仙人峽。隴西郡舊渭州。

translations.literal: Shanggui was formerly called Shanggui and carried Tianshui Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the commandery was restored and the county's name was changed. It had the Meng River. Jicheng was called Jicheng County by Later Zhou and was abolished into Huanggua County. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Jicheng. It had Shigu Cliff. Qingshui was established by Northern Wei, which also established Qingshui Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had barrier offices and Fenshui Ridge. Qinling was established by Northern Wei as Boyang County; during Kaihuang it was changed. Longcheng was formerly called Lüeyang and had Lüeyang Commandery established there. In Kaihuang year two the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Heyang; in year six it was changed to Longcheng. Chengji had long been abolished and was established by Later Zhou. It had Longma City and Xianren Gorge. Longxi Commandery was formerly Weizhou.

translations.literal: Chengji, Longxi Commandery: Longxi Commandery—formerly Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengji. Longxi Commandery: formerly known as Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣五，戶一萬九千二百四十七。

translations.literal: It governed five counties, with nineteen thousand two hundred and forty-seven households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised five counties with nineteen thousand two hundred and forty-seven households.

sentences.zh: 襄武帶郡。隴西舊城內陶，置南安郡。開皇初郡廢，改為武陽，十年改名焉。渭源有鳥鼠山。有渭水。障後魏置。西魏置廣安郡，後周郡廢。長川後魏置安陽郡，領安陽、烏水二縣。西魏改曰北秦州，後又改曰交州。開皇三年郡廢。十八年改州曰紀州，安陽曰長川。大業初州廢，又廢烏水入焉。金城郡開皇初，置蘭州總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Xiangwu carried the commandery. Longxi was the old city of Neitao and had Nan'an Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and it was changed to Wuyang; in year ten its name was changed. Weiyuan had Niaoshu Mountain and the Wei River. Zhang was established by Northern Wei. Western Wei established Guang'an Commandery, which Later Zhou abolished. Changchuan had Anyang Commandery established by Northern Wei, governing Anyang and Wushui counties. Western Wei changed it to Northern Qinzhou, and later again changed it to Jiaozhou. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the province was changed to Jizhou and Anyang to Changchuan. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Wushui was also abolished into it. Jincheng Commandery had the Lanzhou grand administrative office established at the beginning of Kaihuang, and at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 長川金城郡金城郡開皇初，置蘭州總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Changchuan, Jincheng Commandery: Jincheng Commandery—in the beginning of Kaihuang, Lanzhou grand protectorate was established; at the beginning of Daye the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Changchuan. Jincheng Commandery: at the beginning of Kaihuang the Lanzhou grand protectorate was established here; it was abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣二，戶六千八百一十八。

translations.literal: It governed two counties, with six thousand eight hundred and eighteen households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised two counties with six thousand eight hundred and eighteen households.

sentences.zh: 狄道枹罕郡枹罕郡舊置河州。

translations.literal: Didao, Fuhan Commandery: Fuhan Commandery—formerly Hezhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Didao. Fuhan Commandery: Hezhou had formerly been established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶一萬三千一百五十七。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with thirteen thousand one hundred and fifty-seven households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with thirteen thousand one hundred and fifty-seven households.

sentences.zh: 水池澆河郡澆河郡後周武帝逐吐谷渾，以置廓州總管府。

translations.literal: Shuichi, Jiaohe Commandery: Jiaohe Commandery—when Emperor Wu of Zhou drove out Tuyuhun, Kuozhou grand protectorate was established.
translations.idiomatic: Shuichi. Jiaohe Commandery: when Emperor Wu of Zhou drove out Tuyuhun, the Kuozhou grand protectorate was established here.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 統縣二，戶二千二百四十。

translations.literal: It governed two counties, with two thousand two hundred and forty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised two counties with two thousand two hundred and forty households.

sentences.zh: 達化西平郡西平郡舊置鄯州。

translations.literal: Dahua, Xiping Commandery: Xiping Commandery—formerly Shanzhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Dahua. Xiping Commandery: Shanzhou had formerly been established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣二，戶三千一百一十八。

translations.literal: It governed two counties, with three thousand one hundred and eighteen households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised two counties with three thousand one hundred and eighteen households.

sentences.zh: 湟水舊曰西都，後周置樂都郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年改縣曰湟水。又有舊浩亹縣，又西魏置龍居、路倉二縣，並後周廢。大業初置西平郡。有土樓山。化隆舊魏曰廣威，西魏置澆河郡，後周廢郡，仁壽初改為化隆，有拔延山、湟水、盧水。武威郡舊涼州，後周置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Huangshui was formerly called Xidu; Later Zhou established Ledu Commandery there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county was changed to Huangshui. It also had the old Haomen County, and Western Wei also established Longju and Lucang counties; all were abolished by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Daye, Xiping Commandery was established. It had Tulou Mountain. Hualong was called Guangwei by the old Wei; Western Wei established Jiaohe Commandery, Later Zhou abolished the commandery, and at the beginning of Renshou it was changed to Hualong. It had Bayan Mountain, the Huang River, and the Lu River. Wuwei Commandery was formerly Liangzhou; Later Zhou established a grand administrative office, and at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 化隆武威郡武威郡舊涼州，後周置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Hualong, Wuwei Commandery: Wuwei Commandery—formerly Liangzhou; Later Zhou established a grand protectorate, abolished at the beginning of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong. Wuwei Commandery: formerly Liangzhou; Later Zhou set up a grand protectorate here, abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶一萬一千七百五。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with eleven thousand seven hundred and five households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with eleven thousand seven hundred and five households.

sentences.zh: 姑臧舊置武威郡，開皇初郡廢。大業初複置武威郡。又後魏置武安郡、襄武縣，並西魏廢。又舊有顯美縣，後周廢。有茅五山。昌松後魏置昌松郡，後周廢郡，以榆次縣入。開皇初改縣為永世，後改曰昌松。又有後魏魏安郡，後周改置白山縣，尋廢。有白山。番和後魏置番和郡。後周郡廢，置鎮。開皇中為縣，又並力乾、安寧、廣城、障、燕支五縣之地入焉。有燕支山。允吾後魏置，曰廣武，及置廣武郡。開皇初郡廢，改縣曰邑次，尋改為廣武，後又改為邑次。大業初改為允吾。有青岩山。張掖郡西魏置西涼州，尋改曰甘州。

translations.literal: Guzang formerly had Wuwei Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Wuwei Commandery was restored. Northern Wei also established Wu'an Commandery and Xiangwu County, both abolished by Western Wei. It also formerly had Xianmei County, which Later Zhou abolished. It had Maowu Mountain. Changsong had Changsong Commandery established by Northern Wei; Later Zhou abolished the commandery and merged Yuci County into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the county was changed to Yongshi, and later changed to Changsong. It also had Northern Wei's Wei'an Commandery; Later Zhou changed it to establish Baishan County, which was soon abolished. It had Bai Mountain. Fanhe had Fanhe Commandery established by Northern Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and established a garrison. During Kaihuang it became a county, and the lands of Liqian, Anning, Guangcheng, Zhang, and Yanzhi counties were also merged into it. It had Yanzhi Mountain. Yunwu was established by Northern Wei as Guangwu, and Guangwu Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Yici; soon it was changed to Guangwu, and later again changed to Yici. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Yunwu. It had Qingyan Mountain. Zhangye Commandery had Western Liangzhou established by Western Wei, soon changed to Ganzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Yunwu. Zhangye Commandery: the Western Wei established Western Liangzhou here, soon renamed Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶六千一百二十六。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with six thousand one hundred and twenty-six households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with six thousand one hundred and twenty-six households.

sentences.zh: 張掖舊曰永平縣，後周置張掖郡。開皇初郡廢，十七年縣改為酒泉。大業初改為張掖，置張掖郡。又有臨松縣，後周廢。有甘峻山、臨松山、合黎山、有玉石澗、大柳谷。刪丹後魏曰山丹，又有西郡、永寧縣。西魏郡廢，縣改為弱水。後周省入山丹。大業改為刪丹。又後周置金山縣，尋廢入焉。有祀山。有鹽池。有溺水。福祿舊置酒泉郡，開皇初郡廢。仁壽中以置肅州，大業初州尋廢，又後周置樂涫縣，尋廢。有祁連山，崆峒山、昆侖山，有石渠。敦煌郡舊置瓜州。

translations.literal: Zhangye was formerly called Yongping County; Later Zhou established Zhangye Commandery there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year seventeen the county was changed to Jiuquan. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Zhangye, and Zhangye Commandery was established. It also had Linsong County, which Later Zhou abolished. It had Ganjun Mountain, Linsong Mountain, Heli Mountain, Yushi Ravine, and Daliu Valley. Shandan was called Shandan by Northern Wei and also had Western Commandery and Yongning County. Western Wei abolished the commandery and changed the county to Ruoshui. Later Zhou abolished it into Shandan. Daye changed it to Shandan. Later Zhou also established Jinshan County, which was soon abolished into it. It had Si Mountain, salt ponds, and the Ni River. Fulu formerly had Jiuquan Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. During Renshou, Suzhou was established there; at the beginning of Daye the province was soon abolished. Later Zhou also established Leguan County, soon abolished. It had Qilian Mountain, Kongtong Mountain, Kunlun Mountain, and Shiqu. Dunhuang Commandery formerly had Guazhou established there.

sentences.zh: 福祿敦煌郡敦煌郡舊置瓜州。

translations.idiomatic: Fulu. Dunhuang Commandery: Guazhou had formerly been established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶七千七百七十九。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with seven thousand seven hundred and seventy-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with seven thousand seven hundred and seventy-nine households.

sentences.zh: 敦煌舊置敦煌郡，後周並效穀、壽皇二郡入焉。又並敦煌、鳴沙、平康、效穀、東鄉、龍勒六縣為鳴沙縣。開皇初郡廢。大業置敦煌郡，改鳴沙為敦煌。有神沙山、三危山，有流沙。常樂後魏置常樂郡。後周並涼興、大至、冥安、閏泉，合為涼興縣。開皇初郡廢，改縣為常樂。有關官。玉門後魏置會稽郡。後周廢郡，並會稽、新鄉、延興為會稽縣。開皇中改為玉門，並得後魏玉門郡地。鄯善郡大業五年平吐谷渾置，置在鄯善城，即古樓蘭城也。

translations.literal: Dunhuang formerly had Dunhuang Commandery established there; Later Zhou merged Xiaogu and Shouhuang commanderies into it. It also combined the six counties Dunhuang, Mingsha, Pingkang, Xiaogu, Dongxiang, and Longle to make Mingsha County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. During Daye, Dunhuang Commandery was established and Mingsha was changed to Dunhuang. It had Shensha Mountain, Sanwei Mountain, and flowing sands. Changle had Changle Commandery established by Northern Wei. Later Zhou merged Liangxing, Dazhi, Ming'an, and Runquan to make Liangxing County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Changle. It had barrier offices. Yumen had Kuaiji Commandery established by Northern Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and combined Kuaiji, Xinxiang, and Yanxing as Kuaiji County. During Kaihuang it was changed to Yumen and also obtained the land of Northern Wei's Yumen Commandery. Shanshan Commandery was established in Daye year five after Tuyuhun was pacified. It was established at Shanshan City, which was the ancient city of Loulan.

sentences.zh: 玉門鄯善郡鄯善郡平吐谷渾置，置在鄯善城，即古樓蘭城也。

translations.literal: Yumen, Shanshan Commandery: Shanshan Commandery—established after pacifying Tuyuhun, located at Shanshan city, the ancient Loulan city.
translations.idiomatic: Yumen. Shanshan Commandery: established after pacifying Tuyuhun, located at Shanshan city—the ancient Loulan city.

sentences.zh: 並置且末、西海、河源，總四郡。

translations.literal: Qiemo, Xihai, and Heyuan were also established, four commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qiemo, Xihai, and Heyuan were also established, making four commanderies in all.

translations.literal: There is Puchang Lake and the Shanshan River.
translations.idiomatic: The region includes Puchang Lake and the Shanshan River.

sentences.zh: 濟遠且末郡且末郡置在古且末城。

translations.literal: Jiyuan, Qiemo Commandery: Qiemo Commandery—established at the ancient Qiemo city.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan. Qiemo Commandery: established at the ancient Qiemo city.

translations.literal: There is the Qiemo River and the Sapi Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The region includes the Qiemo River and the Sapi Marsh.

sentences.zh: 伏戎西海郡西海郡置在古伏俟城，即吐谷渾國都。

translations.literal: Furong, Xihai Commandery: Xihai Commandery—established at the ancient Fuyu city, the capital of the Tuyuhun kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Furong. Xihai Commandery: established at the ancient Fuyu city, capital of the Tuyuhun kingdom.

sentences.zh: 有西王母石窟、青海、鹽池。

translations.literal: There is the Queen Mother of the West stone cave, Qinghai Lake, and the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: The region includes the Queen Mother of the West stone cave, Qinghai Lake, and the salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 威定河源郡河源郡置在古赤水城。

translations.literal: Weiding, Heyuan Commandery: Heyuan Commandery—established at the ancient Chishui city.
translations.idiomatic: Weiding. Heyuan Commandery: established at the ancient Chishui city.

sentences.zh: 有曼頭城、積石山，河所出。

translations.literal: There is Mantou city, Jishi Mountain, where the river rises.
translations.idiomatic: The region includes Mantou city and Jishi Mountain, where the river rises.

translations.literal: There is the Seven Crow Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The region includes the Seven Crow Lake.

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Director of the Regions, states: "Directly west is called Yong Province."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Director of the Regions, states: "Directly west is called Yong Province."

sentences.zh: 上當天文，自東井十度至柳八度，為鶉首。

translations.literal: Above it corresponds to the heavens: from Dongjing 10 degrees to Liu 8 degrees, it is the Quen Shou asterism.
translations.idiomatic: In the heavens above it corresponds to the asterism Quen Shou, from tenth year of Dongjing degrees to eighth year of Liu degrees.

translations.literal: In the earthly branch it falls in Wei, obtaining Qin's territorial allotment.
translations.idiomatic: In the earthly branches it falls under Wei, corresponding to Qin's territorial allotment.

sentences.zh: 考其舊俗，前史言之詳矣。

translations.literal: Examining its old customs, the former histories speak of them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Examining its old customs, the former histories describe them in detail.

sentences.zh: 化于姬德，則閒田而興讓，習於嬴敝，則相稽而反脣。

translations.literal: Transformed by the virtue of the Ji house, they left fields fallow and practiced yielding; accustomed to Qin's decadence, they checked each other and turned their lips outward.
translations.idiomatic: Transformed by the virtue of the Ji house, they left fields fallow and practiced yielding; under Qin's decadence, they checked one another and turned their lips outward.

translations.literal: Is this because the soil differs?
translations.idiomatic: Is this because the soil itself differs?

translations.literal: It is also that government and teaching transform people.
translations.idiomatic: It is also that government and teaching transform the people.

sentences.zh: 京兆王都所在，俗具五方，人物混淆，華戎雜錯。

translations.literal: Jingzhao is where the royal capital stands; its customs combine all five directions, people are mixed together, and Chinese and barbarians are intermingled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao is where the royal capital stands; its customs combine all five directions, people are mixed together, and Chinese and barbarians live side by side.

sentences.zh: 去農從商，爭朝夕之利，遊手為事，競錐刀之末。

translations.literal: They abandon farming to follow commerce, contending for profit from morning to evening; idlers make a living competing for the smallest gains.
translations.idiomatic: They abandon farming for commerce, contending for profit from morning to evening; idlers make their living competing for the smallest gains.

sentences.zh: 貴者崇侈靡，賤者薄仁義，豪強者縱橫，貧窶者窘蹙。

translations.literal: The noble pursue extravagance, the lowly slight benevolence and righteousness; the powerful are overbearing, the poor are pressed and squeezed.
translations.idiomatic: The noble pursue extravagance while the lowly slight benevolence and righteousness; the powerful are overbearing and the poor are pressed and squeezed.

sentences.zh: 桴鼓屢驚，盜賊不禁，此乃古今之所同焉。

translations.literal: Drums and gongs are repeatedly alarmed, bandits and thieves are not restrained—this is the same in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and gongs sound the alarm repeatedly, yet bandits and thieves go unrestrained—this has been the same in ancient and modern times.

sentences.zh: 自京城至於外郡，得馮翊、扶風，是漢之三輔。

translations.literal: From the capital to the outer commanderies, Fengyi and Fufeng are the Three Metropolises of Han.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to the outer commanderies, Fengyi and Fufeng formed the Three Metropolises of Han.

translations.literal: Their customs are largely no different from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs differ little from those of the capital.

sentences.zh: 安定、北地、上郡、隴西、天水、金城，于古為六郡之地，其人性猶質直。

translations.literal: Anding, Beidi, Shangjun, Longxi, Tianshui, and Jincheng—in antiquity were the lands of the Six Commanderies; their people are still straightforward by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Anding, Beidi, Shangjun, Longxi, Tianshui, and Jincheng—in antiquity were the lands of the Six Commanderies, and their people remain straightforward by nature.

sentences.zh: 然尚儉約，習仁義，勤於稼穡，多畜牧，無複寇盜矣。

translations.literal: Yet they value frugality, practice benevolence and righteousness, are diligent in farming, and raise much livestock; bandits and robbers no longer appear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they value frugality, practice benevolence and righteousness, are diligent in farming, and raise much livestock; bandits and robbers are no longer seen.

sentences.zh: 雕陰、延安、弘化，連接山胡，性多木強，皆女淫而婦貞，蓋俗然也。

translations.literal: Diaoyin, Yan'an, and Honghua connect with the mountain Hu; their natures are mostly obstinate; all have promiscuous women yet chaste wives—it is simply their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoyin, Yan'an, and Honghua connect with the mountain Hu; their natures are mostly obstinate; women are promiscuous yet wives remain chaste—it is simply their custom.

sentences.zh: 平涼、朔方、鹽川、靈武、榆林、五原，地接邊荒，多尚武節，亦習俗然焉。

translations.literal: Pingliang, Shuofang, Yanchuan, Lingwu, Yulin, and Wuyuan border on the wilderness; they greatly honor martial spirit—it is also their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang, Shuofang, Yanchuan, Lingwu, Yulin, and Wuyuan border on the wilderness and greatly honor martial spirit—it is also their custom.

sentences.zh: 河西諸郡，其風頗同，並有金方之氣矣。

translations.literal: The commanderies west of the river—their customs are quite similar, and all possess the qi of the Metal Direction.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies west of the river share similar customs, and all possess the qi of the Metal Direction.

sentences.zh: 梁州漢川郡漢川郡舊置梁州。

translations.literal: Liang Province, Hanchuan Commandery: Hanchuan Commandery—formerly Liangzhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Province, Hanchuan Commandery: Hanchuan Commandery—Liangzhou had formerly been established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶一萬一千九百一十。

translations.literal: It governed eight counties, with eleven thousand nine hundred and ten households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eight counties with eleven thousand nine hundred and ten households.

sentences.zh: 南鄭舊置漢川郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初置郡。又西魏置白雲縣，至是併入焉。有黃牛山、龍岡山。西舊曰勣塚，大業初改焉。有關官，有定軍山、百牢山、街亭山、嶓塚山。有漢水。褒城開皇初曰褒內。仁壽九年因失印更給，改名焉。有關官。有女郎山。城固興勢舊置儻城郡，開皇初郡廢。西鄉舊曰豐寧，置洋州及洋川郡。開皇初廢郡，大業初廢州，改縣曰西鄉。又舊有懷昌郡，後周廢為懷昌縣，至是入焉。有洋水。黃金難江後周置集州及平桑郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢。西城郡梁置梁州，尋改曰南梁州。

translations.literal: Nanzheng formerly had Hanchuan Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the commandery was established. Western Wei also established Baiyun County, which by this time was merged into it. It had Huangniu Mountain and Longgang Mountain. Xi was formerly called Jizhong; at the beginning of Daye it was changed. It had barrier offices, Dingjun Mountain, Bailao Mountain, Jieting Mountain, Bozhong Mountain, and the Han River. Baocheng was called Baonei at the beginning of Kaihuang. In Renshou year nine, because its seal was lost and a replacement was issued, the name was changed. It had barrier offices and Nulang Mountain. Chenggu and Xingshi formerly had Tangcheng Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Xixiang was formerly called Fengning and had Yangzhou and Yangchuan Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished and the county was changed to Xixiang. It also formerly had Huaichang Commandery; Later Zhou abolished it to become Huaichang County, and by this time it entered Xixiang. It had the Yang River. Huangjin and Nanjiang had Jizhou and Pingsang Commandery established by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Xicheng Commandery had Liangzhou established by Liang, soon changed to Southern Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 難江西城郡西城郡梁置梁州，尋改曰南梁州。

translations.literal: Nanjiang, Xicheng Commandery: Xicheng Commandery—Liang established Liangzhou, soon changed to Southern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjiang. Xicheng Commandery: Liang established Liangzhou here, soon renamed Southern Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 西魏改置東梁州，尋改為金州，置總管府。

translations.literal: The Western Wei changed it to Eastern Liangzhou, soon changed to Jinzhou, and established a grand protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei renamed it Eastern Liangzhou, then Jinzhou, and established a grand protectorate.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 統縣六，戶一萬四千三百四十一。

translations.literal: It governed six counties, with fourteen thousand three hundred and forty-one households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised six counties with fourteen thousand three hundred and forty-one households.

sentences.zh: 金川梁初曰上廉，後曰吉陽。西魏改曰吉安，後周以西城入焉。舊有金城、吉安二郡，開皇初並廢。十八年改縣為吉安。大業三年改曰金川，置西城郡。又後周置洵州，尋廢。有焦陵山。石泉舊曰永樂，置晉昌郡。西魏改郡曰魏昌，尋改永樂曰石泉，析置魏寧縣。後周省魏昌郡入中城郡，又省魏甯縣入石泉縣。洵陽舊置洵陽郡，開皇初郡廢。有洵水。安康舊曰甯都，齊置安康郡，後魏置東梁州，後蕭詧改直州。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢，縣改曰安康。黃土西魏置涓陽郡。後周改郡，置縣曰長岡。後郡省入甲郡，置縣曰黃土，並赤石、甲、臨江三縣入焉。開皇初郡廢。豐利梁置南上洛郡，西魏改郡曰豐利。後周省郡入上津郡，以熊川、陽川二縣入豐利。後又廢上津郡入甲郡。有天心水。房陵郡西魏置光遷國。

translations.literal: Jinchuan was called Shanglian at the beginning of Liang and later Jiyang. Western Wei changed it to Ji'an, and Later Zhou merged Xicheng into it. It formerly had Jincheng and Ji'an commanderies, both abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. In year eighteen the county was changed to Ji'an. In Daye year three it was changed to Jinchuan, and Xicheng Commandery was established. Later Zhou also established Xunzhou, which was soon abolished. It had Jiaoling Mountain. Shiquan was formerly called Yongle and had Jinchang Commandery established there. Western Wei changed the commandery to Weichang, soon changed Yongle to Shiquan, and divided off and established Weining County. Later Zhou abolished Weichang Commandery into Zhongcheng Commandery and also abolished Weining County into Shiquan County. Xunyang formerly had Xunyang Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had the Xun River. Ankang was formerly called Ningdu; Qi established Ankang Commandery; Later Wei established Eastern Liangzhou; later Xiao Cha changed it to Zhizhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and the county was changed to Ankang. Huangtu had Juanyang Commandery established by Western Wei. Later Zhou changed the commandery and established a county called Changgang. Later the commandery was abolished into Jia Commandery, and a county called Huangtu was established; Chishi, Jia, and Linjiang counties were merged into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Fengli had Southern Shangluo Commandery established by Liang; Western Wei changed the commandery to Fengli. Later Zhou abolished the commandery into Shangjin Commandery and merged Xiongchuan and Yangchuan counties into Fengli. Later it also abolished Shangjin Commandery into Jia Commandery. It had Tianxin River. Fangling Commandery had the Guangqian kingdom established by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 豐利房陵郡房陵郡西魏置光遷國。

translations.literal: Fengli, Fangling Commandery: Fangling Commandery—the Western Wei established Guangqian Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Fengli. Fangling Commandery: the Western Wei established the Guangqian Principality here.

translations.literal: Later Zhou abolished the principality and established Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou abolished the principality and established Qianzhou.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye it was renamed Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye it was renamed Fangzhou.

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with seven thousand one hundred and six households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with seven thousand one hundred and six households.

sentences.zh: 光遷舊曰房陵，置新城郡。梁末置岐州，後周郡縣並改為光遷，又有舊綏州，開皇初，與郡並廢。大業初置房陵郡。有房山、霍水。永清舊曰大洪，後周改焉。有照珠山、百武山、沮水、泛水。竹山梁曰安城，西魏改焉。置羅州。開皇十八年改曰房州，大業初州廢。有花林山、懸鼓山。上庸梁曰新豐，西魏改焉。後周改曰孔陽。開皇十八年複曰上庸。清化郡置巴州。

translations.literal: Guangqian was formerly called Fangling and had Xincheng Commandery established there. At the end of Liang, Qizhou was established; Later Zhou changed both commandery and county to Guangqian. It also had old Suizhou, which at the beginning of Kaihuang was abolished together with the commandery. At the beginning of Daye, Fangling Commandery was established. It had Fang Mountain and the Huo River. Yongqing was formerly called Dahong; Later Zhou changed it. It had Zhaozhu Mountain, Baiwu Mountain, the Ju River, and the Fan River. Zhushan was called Ancheng by Liang; Western Wei changed it and established Luozhou. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Fangzhou, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Hualin Mountain and Xuangu Mountain. Shangyong was called Xinfeng by Liang; Western Wei changed it. Later Zhou changed it to Kongyang. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was again called Shangyong. Qinghua Commandery had Bazhou established.

sentences.zh: 上庸清化郡清化郡置巴州。

translations.literal: Shangyong, Qinghua Commandery: Qinghua Commandery—Bazhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyong. Qinghua Commandery: Bazhou was established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣十四，戶一萬六千五百三十九。

translations.literal: It governed fourteen counties, with sixteen thousand five hundred and thirty-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised fourteen counties with sixteen thousand five hundred and thirty-nine households.

sentences.zh: 化成梁曰梁廣，仍置歸化郡。後周改縣曰化成。開皇初郡廢。大業初置清化郡。曾口梁置。清化梁置，曰伏強，有木門郡。開皇三年郡廢，七年縣改曰清化。有伏強山。清水盤道梁置，曰難江。西魏改焉。有龍腹山。永穆梁置，曰永康，又有萬榮郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。歸仁梁置，曰平州縣。後周改曰同昌，開皇中改名焉。始甯梁置，並置遂寧郡。開皇初郡廢。有始寧山。其章梁置。恩陽梁置，曰義陽。開皇末改。長池後周置，曰曲細。開皇末改焉。符陽舊置其章郡，開皇初廢。白石有文山。安固梁置。後周置蓬州，大業初州廢。有大蓬山。伏虞梁置，曰宣漢，及置伏虞郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年改焉。通川郡梁置萬州，西魏曰通州。

translations.literal: Huacheng was called Liangguang by Liang, which still established Guihua Commandery there. Later Zhou changed the county to Huacheng. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Qinghua Commandery was established. Zengkou was established by Liang. Qinghua was established by Liang as Fuqiang, and had Mumen Commandery. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished, and in year seven the county was changed to Qinghua. It had Fuqiang Mountain. Qingshui and Pandao were established by Liang as Nanjiang. Western Wei changed them. It had Longfu Mountain. Yongmu was established by Liang as Yongkang, and it also had Wanrong Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. Guiren was established by Liang as Pingzhou County. Later Zhou changed it to Tongchang, and during Kaihuang its name was changed. Shining was established by Liang, which also established Suining Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Shining Mountain. Qizhang was established by Liang. Enyang was established by Liang as Yiyang; at the end of Kaihuang it was changed. Changchi was established by Later Zhou as Quxi; at the end of Kaihuang it was changed. Fuyang formerly had Qizhang Commandery established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Baishi had Wen Mountain. Angu was established by Liang. Later Zhou established Pengzhou, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Dapeng Mountain. Fuyu was established by Liang as Xuanhan, and Fuyu Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen it was changed. Tongchuan Commandery had Wanzhou established by Liang; Western Wei called it Tongzhou.

translations.literal: Fuyu, Tongchuan Commandery: Tongchuan Commandery—Liang established Wanzhou; the Western Wei called it Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu. Tongchuan Commandery: Liang established Wanzhou here; the Western Wei renamed it Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戶一萬二千六百二十四。

translations.literal: It governed seven counties, with twelve thousand six hundred and twenty-four households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised seven counties with twelve thousand six hundred and twenty-four households.

sentences.zh: 通川梁曰石城，置東關郡。開皇初郡廢。大業初置通川郡。三岡梁置，屬新安郡。西魏改郡曰新寧。開皇初郡廢。石鼓西魏置遷州。後周廢州，置臨清郡。開皇初廢郡。東鄉西魏置石州，後周廢州，置三巴郡。開皇初郡廢。宣漢西魏置并州及永昌郡。開皇三年郡廢，五年州廢。西流後魏曰漢興。西魏改焉，又置開州，及周安、萬安、江會三郡。後周省江會入周安。開皇初郡並廢，大業初州廢。萬世後周置，及置萬世郡。開皇初郡廢。宕渠郡梁置渠州。

translations.literal: Tongchuan was called Shicheng by Liang, which established Dongguan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Tongchuan Commandery was established. Sangang was established by Liang and belonged to Xin'an Commandery. Western Wei changed the commandery to Xinning. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Shigu had Qianzhou established by Western Wei. Later Zhou abolished the province and established Linqing Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Dongxiang had Shizhou established by Western Wei; Later Zhou abolished the province and established Sanba Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Xuanhan had Bingzhou and Yongchang Commandery established by Western Wei. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished, and in year five the province was abolished. Xiliu was called Hanxing by Northern Wei. Western Wei changed it, and also established Kaizhou and the three commanderies Zhou'an, Wan'an, and Jianghui. Later Zhou abolished Jianghui into Zhou'an. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were all abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Wanshi was established by Later Zhou, and Wanshi Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Dangqu Commandery had Quzhou established by Liang.

translations.literal: It governed six counties, with fourteen thousand and thirty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised six counties with fourteen thousand and thirty-five households.

sentences.zh: 流江後魏置縣，及置流江郡，開皇初郡廢，大業初置宕渠郡。賨城舊曰始安。開皇十八年改焉。鄰水梁置縣，並置鄰州，後魏改鄰山郡，開皇初郡廢。宕渠梁置，並置境陽郡。開皇初郡廢。咸安梁置，曰綏安。開皇末改名焉。墊江西魏置縣及容川、容山郡。後周改為魏安縣。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。漢陽郡後魏曰南秦州，西魏曰成州。

translations.literal: Liujiang had a county established by Northern Wei, which also established Liujiang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Dangqu Commandery was established. Zongcheng was formerly called Shi'an; in Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed. Linshui had a county established by Liang, together with Linzhou; Later Wei changed it to Linshan Commandery, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Dangqu was established by Liang, which also established Jingyang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Xian'an was established by Liang as Sui'an; at the end of Kaihuang its name was changed. Dianjiang had a county and Rongchuan and Rongshan commanderies established by Western Wei. Later Zhou changed it to Wei'an County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. Hanyang Commandery was called Southern Qinzhou by Later Wei and Chengzhou by Western Wei.

translations.idiomatic: Dianjiang. Hanyang Commandery: the Northern Wei called it Southern Qinzhou; the Western Wei renamed it Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶一萬九百八十五。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with ten thousand nine hundred and eighty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with ten thousand nine hundred and eighty-five households.

sentences.zh: 上祿舊置仇池郡，後魏置倉泉縣，後周廢階陵、豐川、建平、城階四縣入焉。開皇初郡廢，大業初置漢陽郡，改縣曰上祿。有百頃堆。潭水西魏置潭水郡。後周郡廢，並廢甘若，相山、武定三縣入焉。長道後魏置漢陽郡。後周郡廢，又省水南縣入焉。開皇初郡廢，十八年改曰長道。臨洮郡後周武帝逐吐谷渾，以置洮陽郡，尋立洮州。

translations.literal: Shanglu formerly had Qiuchi Commandery established there. Later Wei established Cangquan County; Later Zhou abolished Jieling, Fengchuan, Jianping, and Chengjie counties into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye Hanyang Commandery was established and the county was changed to Shanglu. It had Baiqingdui. Tanshui had Tanshui Commandery established by Western Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Ganruo, Xiangshan, and Wuding counties into it. Changdao had Hanyang Commandery established by Later Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Shuinan County into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen it was changed to Changdao. Lintao Commandery was created when Emperor Wu of Later Zhou drove out Tuyuhun and established Taoyang Commandery; soon Taozhou was established.

translations.idiomatic: Changdao. Lintao Commandery: when Emperor Wu of Zhou drove out Tuyuhun, Taoyang Commandery was established here, and Taozhou was soon established.

translations.idiomatic: The commandery was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戶二萬八千九百七十一。

translations.literal: It governed eleven counties, with twenty-eight thousand nine hundred and seventy-one households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eleven counties with twenty-eight thousand nine hundred and seventy-one households.

sentences.zh: 美相後周置縣，及置洮陽郡。開皇初郡廢，並洮陽縣入焉。大業初置監洮郡。疊川後周置疊州、疊川縣。開皇四年置總管府，大業元年府廢。有洮水、流水。合川後周置，仍立西疆郡。開皇初郡廢。有白嶺山。樂川後周置。歸政開皇二年置，仍立疆澤郡，三年廢，又後周立弘州及開遠、河濱二郡。開皇初州郡並廢。洮源後周置，曰金城，並立旭州，又置通義郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改為美俗。大業初州廢，縣改名焉。洮陽後周置，曰廣恩，並置廣恩郡。開皇初郡廢，仁壽元年，改縣為洮河，大業初改曰洮陽。臨潭後周曰泛潭，開皇十一年改名焉。臨洮西魏置，曰溢樂，並置岷州及同和郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢，更名縣曰臨洮。又後周置祐川郡、基城縣，尋郡縣俱廢。有岷山、崆峒山。當夷後周置。又立洪和郡，郡尋廢。又置博陵郡及博陵、寧人二縣。開皇初併入。和政後周置洮城郡，尋廢。宕昌郡後周置宕昌國，天和元年置宕州總管府。開皇四年府廢。

translations.literal: Meixiang had a county and Taoyang Commandery established by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Taoyang County was merged into it. At the beginning of Daye, Jiantao Commandery was established. Diechuan had Diezhou and Diechuan County established by Later Zhou. In Kaihuang year four a grand administrative office was established, and in Daye year one the office was abolished. It had the Tao River and Liu River. Hechuan was established by Later Zhou, which still established Xijiang Commandery there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Bailing Mountain. Lechuan was established by Later Zhou. Guizheng was established in Kaihuang year two, and Jiangze Commandery was still established there; in year three it was abolished. Later Zhou also established Hongzhou and Kaiyuan and Hebin commanderies. At the beginning of Kaihuang the province and commanderies were all abolished. Taoyuan was established by Later Zhou as Jincheng; Xuzhou was also established, and Tongyi Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county was changed to Meisu. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished and the county's name was changed. Taoyang was established by Later Zhou as Guang'en, and Guang'en Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in Renshou year one the county was changed to Taohe, and at the beginning of Daye it was changed to Taoyang. Lintan was called Fantan by Later Zhou; in Kaihuang year eleven its name was changed. Lintao was established by Western Wei as Yile, with Minzhou and Tonghe Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and the county was renamed Lintao. Later Zhou also established Youchuan Commandery and Jicheng County; soon both commandery and county were abolished. It had Min Mountain and Kongtong Mountain. Dangyi was established by Later Zhou. Honghe Commandery was also established, soon abolished. Boling Commandery and Boling and Ningren counties were also established; at the beginning of Kaihuang they were merged into it. Hezheng had Taocheng Commandery established by Later Zhou, soon abolished. Dangchang Commandery had the Dangchang kingdom established by Later Zhou; in Tianhe year one the Dangzhou grand administrative office was established. In Kaihuang year four the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶六千九百九十六。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with six thousand nine hundred and ninety-six households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with six thousand nine hundred and ninety-six households.

sentences.zh: 懷道武都郡武都郡西魏置武州。

translations.literal: Huaidao, Wudu Commandery: Wudu Commandery—the Western Wei established Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidao. Wudu Commandery: the Western Wei established Wuzhou here.
