translations.literal: It governed seven counties, with ten thousand seven hundred and eighty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised seven counties with ten thousand seven hundred and eighty households.

sentences.zh: 將利舊曰石門，西魏改曰安育。後周改曰將利，置武都郡，後改曰永都郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初置武都郡。又有東平縣，後周併入焉。有河池水。建威後魏置白水郡，郡廢，改為白水縣。西魏複立郡，改為綏戎。後周郡廢，改為建威縣，並廢洪化縣入焉。又西魏有孔堤郡及縣，後周並廢。覆津後魏初曰玩當，置武階郡。西魏又置覆津縣，及置萬郡，統赤萬、接難、五部三縣。後周一郡三縣並玩當，並廢入焉。開皇初武階郡又廢。盤堤西魏置，曰南五部縣，後改名焉；並立武陽郡及茄蘆縣。後周郡廢，縣併入焉。長松西魏置，初曰建昌，置文州及盧北郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改曰長松，大業初州廢。曲水西魏置。正西西魏置。同昌郡西魏逐吐谷渾，置鄧州。開皇七年改曰扶州。

translations.literal: Jiangli was formerly called Shimen; Western Wei changed it to Anyu. Later Zhou changed it to Jiangli, established Wudu Commandery there, and later changed it to Yongdu Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Wudu Commandery was established. It also had Dongping County, which Later Zhou merged into it. It had the Hechi River. Jianwei had Baishui Commandery established by Later Wei; when the commandery was abolished, it was changed to Baishui County. Western Wei restored the commandery and changed it to Suirong. Later Zhou abolished the commandery, changed it to Jianwei County, and abolished Honghua County into it. Western Wei also had Kongdi Commandery and County; Later Zhou abolished both. Fujin was first called Wandang by Later Wei, which established Wujie Commandery there. Western Wei also established Fujin County and Wan Commandery, which governed Chiwan, Jienan, and Wubu counties. Later Zhou abolished the one commandery, three counties, and Wandang into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang, Wujie Commandery was also abolished. Pandi was established by Western Wei as Southern Wubu County and later renamed; Wuyang Commandery and Jialu County were also established. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and merged the county into it. Changsong was established by Western Wei, first called Jianchang, with Wenzhou and Lubei Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, in year eighteen the county was changed to Changsong, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Qushui was established by Western Wei. Zhengxi was established by Western Wei. Tongchang Commandery was created when Western Wei drove out Tuyuhun and established Dengzhou. In Kaihuang year seven it was changed to Fuzhou.

translations.literal: It governed eight counties, with twelve thousand two hundred and forty-eight households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eight counties with twelve thousand two hundred and forty-eight households.

sentences.zh: 尚安西魏置縣及鄧寧郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初置同昌郡。有黑水。鉗川西魏置。有鉗川山。有白水。貼夷西魏置，又置昌寧郡。開皇三年郡廢。同昌西魏置。有鄧至山，雲鄧艾所至，故名焉。嘉誠後周置縣並龍涸郡及扶州總管府。開皇初府廢，三年郡廢，七年州廢。有雪山。封德後魏置，又立芳州，有深泉郡，開皇初郡廢，又省理定縣入焉。大業初州廢。常芬後周置，及立恆香郡。開皇初郡廢。有弱水。金崖後周置。河池郡後魏置南岐州，後周改曰鳳州。

translations.literal: Shang'an had a county and Dengning Commandery established by Western Wei. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Tongchang Commandery was established. It had Blackwater. Qianchuan was established by Western Wei. It had Qianchuan Mountain and whitewater. Tieyi was established by Western Wei, which also established Changning Commandery. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished. Tongchang was established by Western Wei. It had Dengzhi Mountain, said to be named because Deng Ai reached it. Jiacheng had a county, Longhe Commandery, and the Fuzhou grand administrative office established by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the office was abolished; in year three the commandery was abolished; in year seven the province was abolished. It had Snow Mountain. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Changfen was established by Later Zhou, which also established Hengxiang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. translations.idiomatic: Jinyai. Hechi Commandery: the Northern Wei established Southern Qizhou here; Later Zhou renamed it Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶一萬一千二百二。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with eleven thousand two hundred and two households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with eleven thousand two hundred and two households.

sentences.zh: 梁泉舊曰故道，後魏置郡，曰固道，縣曰涼泉，尋改曰梁泉。西魏改郡曰歸真。後周廢郡，又廢龍安、商樂二縣入。大業初置郡。兩當後魏置，及立兩當郡。開皇初郡廢。河池後魏曰廣化，並置廣化郡。開皇初郡廢，仁壽初縣改名焉。又後魏置思安縣，大業初省入。有河池水。同谷舊曰白石，置廣業郡。西魏改曰同穀，後周置康州。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢。又有泥陽縣，西魏廢。順政郡後魏置東益州，梁為武興蕃王國，西魏改為興州。

translations.literal: Liangquan was formerly called Gudao. Later Wei established a commandery called Gudao there, while the county was called Liangquan; soon it was changed to Liangquan. Western Wei changed the commandery to Guizhen. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Long'an and Shangle counties into it. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was established. Liangdang was established by Later Wei, which also established Liangdang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Hechi was called Guanghua by Later Wei, which also established Guanghua Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Renshou the county's name was changed. Later Wei also established Si'an County, which was abolished into it at the beginning of Daye. It had the Hechi River. Tonggu was formerly called Baishi and had Guangye Commandery established there. Western Wei changed it to Tonggu, and Later Zhou established Kangzhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It also had Niyang County, which Western Wei abolished. Shunzheng Commandery had Eastern Yizhou established by Later Wei; Liang made it the Wuxing frontier kingdom; Western Wei changed it to Xingzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Tonggu. Shunzheng Commandery: the Northern Wei established Eastern Yizhou here; Liang made it the Wuxing Barbarian Kingdom; the Western Wei renamed it Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶四千二百六十一。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with four thousand two hundred and sixty-one households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with four thousand two hundred and sixty-one households.

sentences.zh: 順政舊曰略陽。西魏置郡，曰順政，縣曰漢曲；又置仇池縣，後改曰靈道。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。大業初置郡，又省靈道縣併入。鳴水西魏置，曰落叢，並置落叢郡。開皇初郡廢。六年，縣改為廚北。八年，改曰鳴水。長舉西魏置，又立盤頭郡。後周廢郡，有鳳溪水。修城舊置修城郡，縣曰廣長。後周郡廢；又廢下阪縣入。仁壽初，縣改名焉。又西魏置柏樹縣，後周廢。義城郡後魏立益州，世號小益州。

translations.literal: Shunzheng was formerly called Lüeyang. Western Wei established a commandery called Shunzheng, while the county was called Hanqu; it also established Qiuchi County, later changed to Lingdao. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was established, and Lingdao County was also abolished and merged into it. Mingshui was established by Western Wei as Luocong, and Luocong Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year six the county was changed to Chubei. In year eight it was changed to Mingshui. Changju was established by Western Wei, which also established Pantou Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery. It had Fengxi River. Xiucheng formerly had Xiucheng Commandery established there, while the county was called Guangchang. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Xiaban County into it. At the beginning of Renshou the county's name was changed. Western Wei also established Baishu County, which Later Zhou abolished. Yicheng Commandery had Yizhou established by Later Wei; in its time it was called Little Yizhou.

translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng. Yicheng Commandery: the Northern Wei established Yizhou here, known as Lesser Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 西魏複曰益州，又改曰利州，置總管府。

translations.literal: The Western Wei again called it Yizhou, then changed it to Lizhou and established a grand protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei restored the name Yizhou, then changed it to Lizhou and established a grand protectorate.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate was abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戶一萬五千九百五十。

translations.literal: It governed seven counties, with fifteen thousand nine hundred and fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised seven counties with fifteen thousand nine hundred and fifty households.

sentences.zh: 綿谷舊曰興安，置晉壽郡。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。大業初置郡。又有華陽郡，梁置華州，西魏並廢。有龍門山。益昌義城西魏置。葭萌後魏曰晉安，置新巴郡。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。大業初又並恩金縣入焉。岐坪景穀舊曰白水，置平興郡。後周省東洛郡入。開皇初郡廢，縣改名平興。十八年，改曰景穀。大業初又省魚般縣入焉。有關官。有木馬山、良珠山。有凍水。嘉川舊置宋熙郡，開皇初廢。平武郡西魏置龍州。

translations.literal: Miangu was formerly called Xing'an and had Jinshou Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was established. It also had Huayang Commandery; Liang established Huazhou, and Western Wei abolished both. It had Longmen Mountain. Yichang and Yicheng were established by Western Wei. Jiameng was called Jin'an by Later Wei, which established Xinba Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye, Enjin County was also merged into it. Qiping and Jinggu were formerly called Baishui and had Pingxing Commandery established there. Later Zhou abolished Dongluo Commandery into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Pingxing. In year eighteen it was changed to Jinggu. At the beginning of Daye, Yuban County was also abolished into it. It had barrier offices, Muma Mountain, Liangzhu Mountain, and frozen water. Jiachuan formerly had Songxi Commandery established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Pingwu Commandery had Longzhou established by Western Wei.

translations.literal: Jiachuan, Pingwu Commandery: Pingwu Commandery—the Western Wei established Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiachuan. Pingwu Commandery: the Western Wei established Longzhou here.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶五千四百二十。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with five thousand four hundred and twenty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with five thousand four hundred and twenty households.

sentences.zh: 江油後魏置江油郡，開皇三年郡廢，大業初置郡。有關官。馬盤後魏置馬盤郡，開皇三年郡廢。平武梁末，李文智自立為籓王，西魏廢為縣，有涪水、潺水。方維舊曰秦興，置建陽郡。開皇初郡廢，縣改名焉。汶山郡後周置汶州。

translations.literal: Jiangyou had Jiangyou Commandery established by Later Wei; in Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the commandery was established. It had barrier offices. Mapan had Mapan Commandery established by Later Wei, which was abolished in Kaihuang year three. Pingwu: at the end of Liang, Li Wenzhi established himself as a frontier king; Western Wei abolished it to become a county. It had the Fu River and Chan River. Fangwei was formerly called Qinxing and had Jianyang Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. Wenshan Commandery had Wenzhou established by Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 方維汶山郡汶山郡後周置汶州。

translations.literal: Fangwei, Wenshan Commandery: Wenshan Commandery—Later Zhou established Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fangwei. Wenshan Commandery: Later Zhou established Wenzhou here.

sentences.zh: 開皇初改曰蜀州，尋為會州，置總管府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed to Shuzhou, soon to Huizhou, and a grand protectorate was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang it became Shuzhou, soon Huizhou, and a grand protectorate was established.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate was abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戶二萬四千一百五十九。

translations.literal: It governed eleven counties, with twenty-four thousand one hundred and fifty-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eleven counties with twenty-four thousand one hundred and fifty-nine households.

sentences.zh: 汶山舊曰廣陽。梁改為北部都尉，置繩州、北部郡。後周改曰汶州。開皇初郡廢，仁壽元年改名焉。北川後周置。有龍泉水、鷹門山，襄陽山。汶川後周置汝山郡，開皇初郡廢。交川開皇初置。有關官。通化開皇初置，曰金川，仁壽初改名焉。左封後周置，曰廣年，及置廣年郡、左封郡。開皇初郡並廢。仁壽初縣改名焉。又周置翼州，大業初廢，有汶山。平康後周置。有羊腸山。翼水後周置，曰龍求，及置清江郡。開皇初郡廢，縣改曰清江。十八年，又改名焉。翼針後周置，及翼針郡。開皇初郡廢。有石鏡山。江源後周置。通軌後周置縣及覃州，並覃川、榮鄉二郡。開皇初郡廢，四年州廢。有甘松山。普安郡梁置南梁州，後改為安州，西魏改為始州。

translations.literal: Wenshan was formerly called Guangyang. Liang changed it to the Northern Section Commandant and established Shengzhou and Northern Section Commandery. Later Zhou changed it to Wenzhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in Renshou year one the name was changed. Beichuan was established by Later Zhou. It had Longquan River, Yingmen Mountain, and Xiangyang Mountain. Wenchuan had Rushan Commandery established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Jiaochuan was established at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had barrier offices. Tonghua was established at the beginning of Kaihuang as Jinchuan; at the beginning of Renshou the name was changed. Zuofeng was established by Later Zhou as Guangnian, and Guangnian Commandery and Zuofeng Commandery were established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were both abolished. At the beginning of Renshou the county's name was changed. Zhou also established Yizhou, which was abolished at the beginning of Daye. It had Wenshan. Pingkang was established by Later Zhou. It had Yangchang Mountain. Yishui was established by Later Zhou as Longqiu, and Qingjiang Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Qingjiang. In year eighteen its name was again changed. Yizhen was established by Later Zhou, along with Yizhen Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Shijing Mountain. Jiangyuan was established by Later Zhou. Tonggui had a county and Tanzhou established by Later Zhou, together with Tanchuan and Rongxiang commanderies. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year four the province was abolished. It had Gansong Mountain. Pu'an Commandery had Southern Liangzhou established by Liang; later it was changed to Anzhou, and Western Wei changed it to Shizhou.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties, with thirty-one thousand three hundred and fifty-one households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised seven counties with thirty-one thousand three hundred and fifty-one households.

sentences.zh: 普安舊曰南安。西魏改曰普安，置普安郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初置郡焉。永歸舊曰白水，西魏改焉。黃安舊曰華陽，西魏改焉，又置黃原郡。開皇初郡廢。陰平宋置北陰平郡，魏置龍州。西魏改郡為陰平，又名縣焉。後周從江油郡，改曰靜龍，縣曰陰平。開皇初郡廢。梓潼舊曰安壽，西魏置潼川郡。開皇初郡廢。大業初縣改名焉。有五婦山。武連舊曰武功，置輔劍郡。西魏改郡曰安都，縣曰武連。開皇初郡廢。臨津舊曰胡原。開皇七年改焉。金山郡西魏置潼州。

translations.literal: Pu'an was formerly called Nan'an. Western Wei changed it to Pu'an and established Pu'an Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the commandery was established there. Yonggui was formerly called Baishui; Western Wei changed it. Huang'an was formerly called Huayang; Western Wei changed it and also established Huangyuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Yinping: Song established Northern Yinping Commandery, and Wei established Longzhou. Western Wei changed the commandery to Yinping and also named the county. Later Zhou followed Jiangyou Commandery, changed it to Jinglong, and called the county Yinping. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Zitong was formerly called Anshou; Western Wei established Tongchuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the county's name was changed. It had Wufu Mountain. Wulian was formerly called Wugong and had Fujian Commandery established there. Western Wei changed the commandery to Andu and the county to Wulian. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Linjin was formerly called Huyuan. In Kaihuang year seven it was changed. Jinshan Commandery had Tongzhou established by Western Wei.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties, with thirty-six thousand nine hundred and sixty-three households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised seven counties with thirty-six thousand nine hundred and sixty-three households.

sentences.zh: 巴西舊曰涪，置巴西郡。西魏改縣曰巴西。開皇初郡廢。大業初置金山郡。有鹽井。昌隆有雲臺山。涪城舊置始平郡，西魏改郡為涪城，後周又改曰安城。開皇初郡廢，改縣曰安城。十六年，改為涪城。魏城西魏置。萬安舊曰孱亭，西魏改名焉，置萬安郡。開皇初郡廢。神泉舊曰西充國，開皇六年改名焉。金山舊置益昌、晉興二縣，西魏省晉興入益昌，後周別置金山。開皇四年，省益昌入金山。新城郡梁末置新州。

translations.literal: Baxi was formerly called Fu and had Baxi Commandery established there. Western Wei changed the county to Baxi. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Jinshan Commandery was established. It had salt wells. Changlong had Yuntai Mountain. Fucheng formerly had Shiping Commandery established there; Western Wei changed the commandery to Fucheng, and Later Zhou again changed it to Ancheng. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Ancheng. In year sixteen it was changed to Fucheng. Weicheng was established by Western Wei. Wan'an was formerly called Chanting; Western Wei changed its name and established Wan'an Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Shenquan was formerly called Xichongguo; in Kaihuang year six its name was changed. Jinshan formerly had Yichang and Jinxing counties established there; Western Wei abolished Jinxing into Yichang, and Later Zhou separately established Jinshan. In Kaihuang year four Yichang was abolished into Jinshan. Xincheng Commandery had Xinzhou established at the end of Liang.

sentences.zh: 郪舊曰伍城。西魏改曰昌城，仍置昌城郡。開皇初郡廢。大業初置新城郡，改縣名焉。射洪西魏置，曰射江，後周改名焉。鹽亭西魏置鹽亭郡。開皇初郡廢。有高渠縣。大業初併入焉。通泉舊曰通泉，置西宕渠郡。西魏改郡、縣俱曰勇泉。開皇初郡廢，縣改名，又並光漢縣入焉。飛烏開皇中置。巴西郡梁置南梁、北巴州，西魏置隆州。

translations.literal: Qi was formerly called Wucheng. Western Wei changed it to Changcheng and still established Changcheng Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Xincheng Commandery was established and the county's name was changed. Shehong was established by Western Wei as Shejiang; Later Zhou changed the name. Yanting had Yanting Commandery established by Western Wei. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Gaoqu County, which at the beginning of Daye was merged into it. Tongquan was formerly called Tongquan and had Western Dangqu Commandery established there. Western Wei changed both commandery and county to Yongquan. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, the county's name was changed, and Guanghan County was also merged into it. Feiwu was established during Kaihuang. Baxi Commandery had Southern Liangzhou and Northern Bazhou established by Liang; Western Wei established Longzhou.

Baxi Commandery had Southern Liangzhou and Northern Bazhou established by Liang; Western Wei established Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 飛烏巴西郡巴西郡梁置南梁、北巴州，西魏置隆州。

translations.literal: Feiwu, Baxi Commandery: Baxi Commandery—Liang established Southern Ba and Northern Ba provinces; the Western Wei established Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feiwu. Baxi Commandery: Liang established Southern Ba and Northern Ba provinces here; the Western Wei established Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣十，戶四萬一千六十四。

translations.literal: It governed ten counties, with forty-one thousand and sixty-four households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised ten counties with forty-one thousand and sixty-four households.

sentences.zh: 閬內梁置北巴郡，後魏平蜀，置盤龍郡，開皇初郡廢。大業初置巴西郡。有盤龍山、天柱山、靈山。南部舊曰南充國，梁曰南部，西魏置新安郡，後周郡廢。蒼溪舊曰漢昌，開皇末改名焉。南充舊曰安漢，置宕渠郡。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。相如梁置梓潼郡，後魏郡廢。西水梁置掌天郡，西魏改曰金遷，開皇初郡廢。晉城舊曰西充國，梁置木蘭郡。西魏廢郡，改縣名焉。有閬水。奉國梁置白馬、義陽二郡，開皇初郡廢，並廢義陽縣入焉。儀隴梁置，並置隆城郡。開皇初郡廢。大寅梁置。遂寧郡後周置遂州。

translations.literal: Langnei had Northern Ba Commandery established by Liang. After Later Wei pacified Shu, Panlong Commandery was established, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Baxi Commandery was established. It had Panlong Mountain, Tianzhu Mountain, and Ling Mountain. Cangxi was formerly called Hanchang; at the end of Kaihuang its name was changed. Nanchong was formerly called Anhan and had Dangqu Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the county's name was changed. Xiangru had Zitong Commandery established by Liang, and Later Wei abolished the commandery. Yilong was established by Liang, which also established Longcheng Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Dayin was established by Liang. translations.literal: Dayin, Suining Commandery: Suining Commandery—Later Zhou established Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dayin. Suining Commandery: Later Zhou established Suizhou here.

translations.idiomatic: A grand protectorate was established in the second year of Renshou.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The protectorate was abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶一萬二千六百二十二。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with twelve thousand six hundred and twenty-two households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with twelve thousand six hundred and twenty-two households.

sentences.zh: 方義梁曰小溪，置東遂寧郡。西魏改縣名焉。後周改郡曰石山。開皇初郡廢。大業初置遂寧郡。青石舊曰晉興，西魏改名焉，又置懷化郡。開皇初郡廢。長江舊曰巴興，西魏改名焉，又置懷化郡。開皇初郡廢。涪陵郡西魏置合州。

translations.literal: Fangyi was called Xiaoxi by Liang, which established Eastern Suining Commandery there. Western Wei changed the county's name. Later Zhou changed the commandery to Shishan. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Suining Commandery was established. Qingshi was formerly called Jinxing; Western Wei changed its name and also established Huaihua Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. translations.literal: It governed three counties, with nine thousand nine hundred and twenty-one households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with nine thousand nine hundred and twenty-one households.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶一萬四千四百二十三。

translations.literal: It governed three counties, with fourteen thousand four hundred and twenty-three households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised three counties with fourteen thousand four hundred and twenty-three households.

sentences.zh: 巴舊置巴郡，後周廢枳、墊江二縣入焉。開皇初郡廢。大業初置巴郡。江津舊曰江州縣。西魏改為江陽，置七門郡。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。涪陵舊曰漢平，置涪陵郡。開皇初郡廢。十三年，縣改名焉。巴東郡梁置信州，後周置總管府，大業元年府廢。

translations.literal: It governed fourteen counties, with twenty-one thousand three hundred and seventy households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised fourteen counties with twenty-one thousand three hundred and seventy households.

sentences.zh: 人復舊置巴東郡，縣曰魚複，西魏改曰人複。開皇初郡廢。大業初，置巴東郡。有鹽井、白鹽山。雲安舊曰朐䏰，後周改焉。南浦後周置安鄉郡，後改縣曰安鄉，改郡曰萬川。開皇初郡廢。十八年，縣改名焉。梁山西魏置。有高梁山。有紵溪。大昌後周置永昌郡，尋廢，又廢北井縣入焉。巫山舊置建平郡，開皇初郡廢。有巫山。秭歸後周曰長寧，置秭歸郡。開皇初郡廢，改縣曰秭歸。巴東舊曰歸鄉，梁置信陵郡。後周郡廢，縣改曰樂鄉。開皇末，又改名焉。有巫峽。新浦後周置周安郡，開皇初郡廢。盛山梁曰漢豐，西魏改為永寧，開皇末，曰盛山。臨江梁置臨江郡，後周置臨州。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢。有平都山。有彭溪。武甯後周置南州、南都郡、源陽縣，後改郡曰懷德，縣曰武寧。開皇初州郡並廢入焉。石城開皇初置庸州，大業初州廢。務川開皇末置。蜀郡舊置益州，開皇初廢。

translations.literal: Renfu formerly had Badong Commandery established there, and the county was called Yufu; Western Wei changed it to Renfu. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the county's name was changed. Liangshan was established by Western Wei. It had Gaoliang Mountain and Zhu Brook. Dachang had Yongchang Commandery established by Later Zhou, soon abolished, and Beijing County was also abolished into it. Wushan formerly had Jianping Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Wu Mountain. Zigui was called Changning by Later Zhou and had Zigui Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Zigui. Badong was formerly called Guixiang; Liang established Xinling Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and changed the county to Lexiang. At the end of Kaihuang its name was again changed. It had Wu Gorge. Xinpu had Zhou'an Commandery established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Shengshan was called Hanfeng by Liang; Western Wei changed it to Yongning, and at the end of Kaihuang it was called Shengshan. Linjiang had Linjiang Commandery established by Liang; Later Zhou established Linzhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Pingdu Mountain and Peng Brook. Wuning had Nanzhou, Nandu Commandery, and Yuanyang County established by Later Zhou; later the commandery was changed to Huaide and the county to Wuning. At the beginning of Kaihuang the province and commandery were both abolished into it. Shicheng had Yongzhou established at the beginning of Kaihuang; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Wuchuan was established at the end of Kaihuang. Shu Commandery formerly had Yizhou established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang.

translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou later established a grand protectorate.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，置西南道行台省，三年，複置總管府，大業元年府廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, the Southwest Circuit Executive Office was established; in the third year the grand protectorate was restored; abolished in the first year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang, the Southwest Circuit Executive Office was established; in the third year the grand protectorate was restored, and it was abolished in the first year of Daye.

sentences.zh: 統縣十三，戶十萬五千五百八十六。

translations.literal: It governed thirteen counties, with one hundred and five thousand five hundred and eighty-six households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised thirteen counties with one hundred and five thousand five hundred and eighty-six households.

sentences.zh: 成都舊置蜀郡，又有新都縣。梁置始康郡，西魏廢始康郡。開皇初廢蜀郡，並廢新繁入焉。十八年，改新都曰興樂。大業初置蜀郡，省興樂入焉。舊置懷甯、晉熙、宋興、宋寧四郡，至後周並廢。有武簷山。雙流舊曰廣都，置寧蜀郡，後同郡廢。仁壽元年改縣曰雙流。有女伎山。新津後周置，並置犍為郡。開皇初郡廢。大業初又廢僰道縣入焉。晉原舊曰江原，及置江原郡。後周廢郡，縣改名焉。清城舊置齊基郡，後周廢為清城縣。有鳴鵠山，清城山。九隴舊曰晉壽，梁置東益州。後周州廢，置九隴郡，並改縣曰九隴。仁壽初置濛州。開皇初郡廢，並隴泉、興固，青陽三縣入焉。大業初州廢。有太山、道場山。綿竹舊置晉熙郡及長楊、南武都二縣。後周並二縣為晉熙，後又廢晉熙入陽泉。開皇初郡廢，十八年改為孝水，大業二年改曰綿竹。有冶官。有綿水。有鹿堂山。郫西魏分置溫江縣，開皇初省入。仁壽初複置萬春縣，大業初又廢入焉。有金山、平樂山、天彭門。玄武舊曰伍城，後周置玄武郡。開皇初郡廢，改縣名焉。仁壽初置凱州，大業初廢。有三堆山、郪江。雒舊曰廣漢，又置廣漢郡。開皇初郡廢。十八年，改曰綿竹。大業初改名雒焉。又有西遂甯郡、南陰平郡。後周廢西遂寧，改為懷中，南陰平郡曰南陰平縣，尋並廢。陽安舊曰牛鞞，西魏改名焉，並置武康郡。開皇初郡廢。仁壽初置簡州，大業初州廢。有鹽井。平泉西魏置，曰婆閏。開皇十八年，改名焉金泉西魏置縣及金泉郡。後周廢郡，並廢白牟縣入焉。有昌利山、銅官山、石城山。臨邛郡舊置雅州。

translations.literal: Chengdu formerly had Shu Commandery established there, and also had Xindu County. Liang established Shikang Commandery, and Western Wei abolished Shikang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang, Shu Commandery was abolished, and Xinfan was also abolished into it. In year eighteen, Xindu was changed to Xingle. At the beginning of Daye, Shu Commandery was established and Xingle was abolished into it. It formerly had Huaining, Jinxi, Songxing, and Songning commanderies, all abolished by Later Zhou. It had Wuyan Mountain. Shuangliu was formerly called Guangdu and had Ningshu Commandery established there; later the commandery was also abolished. In Renshou year one the county was changed to Shuangliu. It had Nüji Mountain. Xinjin was established by Later Zhou, which also established Qianwei Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Bodao County was also abolished into it. Jinyuan was formerly called Jiangyuan and had Jiangyuan Commandery established there. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and changed the county's name. Qingcheng formerly had Qiji Commandery established there; Later Zhou abolished it to become Qingcheng County. It had Minghu Mountain and Qingcheng Mountain. Jiulong was formerly called Jinshou; Liang established Eastern Yizhou there. Later Zhou abolished the province, established Jiulong Commandery, and changed the county to Jiulong. At the beginning of Renshou, Mengzhou was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Longquan, Xinggu, and Qingyang counties were merged into it. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Tai Mountain and Daochang Mountain. Mianzhu formerly had Jinxi Commandery and Changyang and Southern Wudu counties established there. Later Zhou merged the two counties as Jinxi, and later abolished Jinxi into Yangquan. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year eighteen it was changed to Xiaoshui, and in Daye year two it was changed to Mianzhu. It had smelting offices, the Mian River, and Lutang Mountain. Pi had Wenjiang County divided off and established by Western Wei; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was abolished into Pi. At the beginning of Renshou, Wanchun County was restored, and at the beginning of Daye it was again abolished into Pi. It had Jin Mountain, Pingle Mountain, and Tianpeng Gate. Xuanwu was formerly called Wucheng; Later Zhou established Xuanwu Commandery there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Renshou, Kaizhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished. It had Sandui Mountain and the Qi River. Luo was formerly called Guanghan, and Guanghan Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen it was changed to Mianzhu, and at the beginning of Daye its name was changed to Luo. It also had Western Suining Commandery and Southern Yinping Commandery. Later Zhou abolished Western Suining, changing it to Huaizhong, and called Southern Yinping Commandery Southern Yinping County; soon both were abolished. Yang'an was formerly called Niubi; Western Wei changed the name and also established Wukang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Renshou, Jianzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had salt wells. Pingquan was established by Western Wei as Porun. In Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. Jinquan had a county and Jinquan Commandery established by Western Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Baimou County into it. It had Changli Mountain, Tongguan Mountain, and Shicheng Mountain. Linqiong Commandery formerly had Yazhou established there.

At the beginning of Renshou, Kaizhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished. It had Sandui Mountain and the Qi River. Luo was formerly called Guanghan, and Guanghan Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen it was changed to Mianzhu, and at the beginning of Daye its name was changed to Luo. It also had Western Suining Commandery and Southern Yinping Commandery. Later Zhou abolished Western Suining, changing it to Huaizhong, and called Southern Yinping Commandery Southern Yinping County; soon both were abolished. Yang'an was formerly called Niubi; Western Wei changed the name and also established Wukang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Renshou, Jianzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had salt wells. Pingquan was established by Western Wei as Porun. In Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. Jinquan had a county and Jinquan Commandery established by Western Wei. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also abolished Baimou County into it. It had Changli Mountain, Tongguan Mountain, and Shicheng Mountain. Linqiong Commandery formerly had Yazhou established there.

sentences.zh: 金泉臨邛郡臨邛郡舊置雅州。

translations.literal: Jinquan, Linqiong Commandery: Linqiong Commandery—formerly Yazhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan. Linqiong Commandery: Yazhou had formerly been established here.

sentences.zh: 統縣九，戶二萬三千三百四十八。

translations.literal: It governed nine counties, with twenty-three thousand three hundred and forty-eight households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised nine counties with twenty-three thousand three hundred and forty-eight households.

sentences.zh: 嚴道西魏置，曰始陽縣，置蒙山郡。開皇初郡廢。十三年，改曰蒙山，尋置雅州。大業置臨邛郡，縣改名焉。有邛來山。名山舊曰蒙山。開皇十三年，改始陽曰蒙山，改蒙山曰名山。盧山仁壽末置。依政西魏置，及置邛州，大業初廢。臨邛舊置臨邛郡，開皇初廢。有火井。蒱江西魏置。曰廣定，及置蒱原郡，開皇初郡廢。仁壽初縣改名焉。蒱溪西魏置。沈黎後周置黎州，尋並縣廢。開皇中置縣。仁壽末置登州，大業初州廢。漢源大業初置。眉山郡西魏曰眉州。

translations.literal: Yandao was established by Western Wei as Shiyang County, and Mengshan Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year thirteen it was changed to Mengshan, and soon Yazhou was established. During Daye, Linqiong Commandery was established and the county's name was changed. It had Qionglai Mountain. Mingshan was formerly called Mengshan. In Kaihuang year thirteen, Shiyang was changed to Mengshan and Mengshan was changed to Mingshan. Lushan was established at the end of Renshou. Yizheng was established by Western Wei, which also established Qiongzhou; at the beginning of Daye it was abolished. Linqiong formerly had Linqiong Commandery established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had fire wells. Pujiang was established by Western Wei as Guangding, and Puyuan Commandery was established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Renshou the county's name was changed. Puxi was established by Western Wei. Shenli had Lizhou established by Later Zhou; soon both the province and county were abolished. During Kaihuang, a county was established. At the end of Renshou, Dengzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Hanyuan was established at the beginning of Daye. Meishan Commandery was called Meizhou by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 漢源眉山郡眉山郡西魏曰眉州。

translations.literal: Hanyuan, Meishan Commandery: Meishan Commandery—the Western Wei called it Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyuan. Meishan Commandery: the Western Wei called it Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 後周曰青州，後又曰嘉州。

translations.literal: Later Zhou called it Qingzhou, then again Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou renamed it Qingzhou, then again Jiazhou.

translations.literal: In the second year of Daye it was again changed to Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daye it was again renamed Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶二萬三千七百九十九。

translations.literal: It governed eight counties, with twenty-three thousand seven hundred and ninety-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised eight counties with twenty-three thousand seven hundred and ninety-nine households.

sentences.zh: 龍遊後周置，曰峨眉，及置平羌郡。開皇初郡廢。九年改縣為青衣。平陳日，龍見水，隨軍而進，十年改名焉。大業初置眉山郡。平羌後周置，仍置平羌郡。開皇初郡廢。夾江開皇三年置。峨眉開皇十三年置。有峨眉山、綏山。通義舊置齊通郡及青州。西魏改州曰眉州。開皇初郡廢，改齊通曰廣通。仁壽元年改為通義。大業初州廢。青神後周置，並置青神郡。開皇初郡廢。丹棱後周置，曰齊樂。開皇中改名焉。洪雅開皇十三年置。隆山郡西魏置陵州。

translations.literal: Longyou was established by Later Zhou as Emei, and Pingqiang Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year nine the county was changed to Qingyi. On the day Chen was pacified, a dragon appeared in the water and advanced with the army; in year ten the name was changed. At the beginning of Daye, Meishan Commandery was established. Pingqiang was established by Later Zhou, and Pingqiang Commandery was still established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Jiajiang was established in Kaihuang year three. Emei was established in Kaihuang year thirteen. It had Emei Mountain and Sui Mountain. Tongyi formerly had Qitong Commandery and Qingzhou established there. Western Wei changed the province to Meizhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and Qitong was changed to Guangtong. In Renshou year one it was changed to Tongyi. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Qingshen was established by Later Zhou, which also established Qingshen Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Danling was established by Later Zhou as Qile; during Kaihuang the name was changed. Hongya was established in Kaihuang year thirteen. Longshan Commandery had Lingzhou established by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 洪雅隆山郡隆山郡西魏置陵州。

translations.literal: Hongya, Longshan Commandery: Longshan Commandery—the Western Wei established Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongya. Longshan Commandery: the Western Wei established Lingzhou here.

sentences.zh: 統縣五，戶一萬一千四十二。

translations.literal: It governed five counties, with eleven thousand and forty-two households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised five counties with eleven thousand and forty-two households.

sentences.zh: 仁壽梁置懷仁郡，西魏改縣曰普寧，開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。又西魏置蒲亭。大業初置隆山郡，蒲亭併入焉。有鹽井。貴平西魏置，又立和仁郡。後周又廢可曇、平井二縣入焉。開皇初郡廢。大業初，又廢籍縣入焉。井研始建開皇十一年置。有鐵山。隆山舊曰犍為，置江州。西魏改縣曰隆山。後周省州，置隆山郡。開皇初郡廢，又並江陽縣入焉。有冶官。有鼎鼻山。資陽郡西魏置資州。

translations.literal: Renshou had Huairen Commandery established by Liang; Western Wei changed the county to Puning. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. Western Wei also established Puting. At the beginning of Daye, Longshan Commandery was established and Puting was merged into it. It had salt wells. Guiping was established by Western Wei, which also established Heren Commandery. Later Zhou also abolished Ketan and Pingjing counties into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Ji County was also abolished into it. Jingyan and Shijian were established in Kaihuang year eleven. It had Iron Mountain. Longshan was formerly called Qianwei and had Jiangzhou established there. Western Wei changed the county to Longshan. Later Zhou abolished the province and established Longshan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Jiangyang County was also merged into it. It had smelting offices and Dingbi Mountain. Ziyang Commandery had Zizhou established by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 隆山資陽郡資陽郡西魏置資州。

translations.literal: Longshan, Ziyang Commandery: Ziyang Commandery—the Western Wei established Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Longshan. Ziyang Commandery: the Western Wei established Zizhou here.

sentences.zh: 統縣九，戶二萬五千七百二十二。

translations.literal: It governed nine counties, with twenty-five thousand seven hundred and twenty-two households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised nine counties with twenty-five thousand seven hundred and twenty-two households.

sentences.zh: 磐石後周置縣及資中郡，開皇初郡廢。大業初置資陽郡。內江後周置。威遠開皇初置。大牢開皇十三年置。安嶽後周置，並置普州。大業初州廢。普慈後周置郡曰普慈，縣曰多業。開皇初郡廢。十三年，縣改名焉。安居後周置，曰柔剛，及置安居郡。開皇初郡廢。十三年，縣改名焉。隆康後周置，曰永康。開皇十八年改焉。資陽後周置。瀘川郡梁置滬州。

translations.literal: Panshi had a county and Zizhong Commandery established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Ziyang Commandery was established. Neijiang was established by Later Zhou. Weiyuan was established at the beginning of Kaihuang. Dalao was established in Kaihuang year thirteen. Anyue was established by Later Zhou, which also established Puzhou. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Puci had a commandery established by Later Zhou called Puci, while the county was called Duoye. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year thirteen the county's name was changed. Anju was established by Later Zhou as Rougang, and Anju Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year thirteen the county's name was changed. Longkang was established by Later Zhou as Yongkang. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed. Ziyang was established by Later Zhou. Luchuan Commandery had Luzhou established by Liang.

Luchuan Commandery had Luzhou established by Liang.

sentences.zh: 資陽瀘川郡瀘川郡梁置滬州。

translations.literal: Ziyang, Luchuan Commandery: Luchuan Commandery—Liang established Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyang. Luchuan Commandery: Liang established Huzhou here.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: During Renshou a grand protectorate was established; at the beginning of Daye the protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A grand protectorate was established during Renshou; it was abolished at the beginning of Daye.

translations.literal: It governed five counties, with one thousand eight hundred and two households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised five counties with one thousand eight hundred and two households.

sentences.zh: 綿水犍為郡犍為郡梁置戎州。

translations.literal: Mianshui, Qianwei Commandery: Qianwei Commandery—Liang established Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mianshui. Qianwei Commandery: Liang established Rongzhou here.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶四千八百五十九。

translations.literal: It governed four counties, with four thousand eight hundred and fifty-nine households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised four counties with four thousand eight hundred and fifty-nine households.

sentences.zh: 僰道後周置，曰外江。大業初改曰僰道，置犍為郡。犍為後周置，曰武陽。開皇初改焉。南溪梁置，曰南廣，及置六同郡。開皇初郡廢。仁壽初縣改名焉。開邊開皇六年置，七年廢訓州入焉。大業初廢恭州、協州入焉。越巂郡後周置嚴州。

translations.literal: Bodao was established by Later Zhou as Waijiang. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Bodao and Qianwei Commandery was established. Qianwei was established by Later Zhou as Wuyang. At the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed. Nanxi was established by Liang as Nanguang, and Liutong Commandery was established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Renshou the county's name was changed. Kaibian was established in Kaihuang year six; in year seven Xunzhou was abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye, Gongzhou and Xiezhou were abolished into it. Yuexi Commandery had Yanzhou established by Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽越巂郡越巂郡後周置嚴州。

translations.literal: Renshou, Yuexi Commandery: Yuexi Commandery—Later Zhou established Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou. Yuexi Commandery: Later Zhou established Yanzhou here.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年改曰西寧州，十八年又改曰巂州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang it was changed to Xiningzhou; in the eighteenth year it was again changed to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang it became Xiningzhou; in the eighteenth year it was again renamed Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣六，戶七千四百四十八。

translations.literal: It governed six counties, with seven thousand four hundred and forty-eight households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised six counties with seven thousand four hundred and forty-eight households.

sentences.zh: 邛部牂柯郡牂柯郡開皇初，置牂。

translations.literal: Qiongbu, Zangke Commandery: Zangke Commandery—at the beginning of Kaihuang, Zang was established.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongbu. Zangke Commandery: at the beginning of Kaihuang Zang was established here.

sentences.zh: 賓化黔安郡黔安郡後周置黔州，不帶郡。

translations.literal: Binhua, Qian'an Commandery: Qian'an Commandery—Later Zhou established Qianzhou, without an attached commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Binhua. Qian'an Commandery: Later Zhou established Qianzhou here, without an attached commandery.

sentences.zh: 統縣二，戶一千四百六十。

translations.literal: It governed two counties, with one thousand four hundred and sixty households.
translations.idiomatic: Its jurisdiction comprised two counties with one thousand four hundred and sixty households.

sentences.zh: 梁州于天官上應參之宿。

translations.literal: Liang Province corresponds above to the lodge of Shen in the celestial offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the celestial offices, Liang Province corresponds above to the lodge of Shen.

translations.literal: In Zhou times Liang Province was merged with Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou dynasty, Liang Province was merged with Yong Province.

translations.literal: Under Han, Yizhou was again separated out.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han dynasty, Yizhou was again separated out.

sentences.zh: 在《禹貢》，自漢川以下諸郡，皆其封域。

translations.literal: In the Tribute of Yu, all the commanderies from Hanchuan downward are within its domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tribute of Yu, all the commanderies from Hanchuan downward fall within its domain.

sentences.zh: 漢中之人，質樸無文，不甚趨利。

translations.literal: The people of Hanzhong are plain and unadorned, not much inclined toward profit.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hanzhong are plain and unadorned, with little inclination toward profit.

sentences.zh: 性嗜口腹，多事田漁，雖蓬室柴門，食必兼肉。

translations.literal: By nature they love food and drink, and are much given to farming and fishing; though they live in thatched huts with brushwood gates, their meals always include meat.
translations.idiomatic: By nature they love food and drink and are much given to farming and fishing; though they live in thatched huts with brushwood gates, their meals always include meat.

sentences.zh: 好祀鬼神，尤多忌諱，家人有死，輒離其故宅。

translations.literal: They greatly honor sacrifices to spirits and are especially full of taboos; when a family member dies, they leave their old dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They greatly honor sacrifices to spirits and are especially full of taboos; when a family member dies, they leave their old dwelling.

sentences.zh: 崇重道教，猶有張魯之風焉。

translations.literal: They deeply revere the Way of the Dao, and still retain the spirit of Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: They deeply revere the Way of the Dao and still retain the spirit of Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 每至五月十五日，必以酒食相饋，賓旅聚會，有甚於三元。

translations.literal: Every year on the fifteenth day of the fifth month they invariably exchange food and drink; travelers gather in assembly, more so than at the Three Primordials festival.
translations.idiomatic: Every year on the fifteenth day of the fifth month they invariably exchange food and drink; travelers gather in assembly, more so than at the Three Primordials festival.

sentences.zh: 傍南山雜有獠戶，富室者頗參夏人為婚，衣服居處言語，殆與華不別。

translations.literal: Along the southern mountains there are mixed Liao households; the wealthy sometimes intermarry with Chinese, and in dress, dwelling, and speech they differ little from the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Along the southern mountains there are mixed Liao households; the wealthy sometimes intermarry with Chinese, and in dress, dwelling, and speech they differ little from the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 西城、房陵、清化、通川、宕渠，地皆連接，風俗頗同。

translations.literal: Xicheng, Fangling, Qinghua, Tongchuan, and Dangqu—their lands all connect, and their customs are quite similar.
translations.idiomatic: Xicheng, Fangling, Qinghua, Tongchuan, and Dangqu—their lands all connect, and their customs are quite similar.

sentences.zh: 漢陽、臨洮、宕昌、武都、同昌、河池，順政、義城、平武、汶山、皆連雜氐羌。

translations.literal: Hanyang, Lintao, Dangchang, Wudu, Tongchang, Hechi, Shunzheng, Yicheng, Pingwu, and Wenshan—all connect with mixed Di and Qiang peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyang, Lintao, Dangchang, Wudu, Tongchang, Hechi, Shunzheng, Yicheng, Pingwu, and Wenshan—all connect with mixed Di and Qiang peoples.

translations.literal: Their people are especially fierce and strong, and by nature mostly straightforward.
translations.idiomatic: Their people are especially fierce and strong, and by nature mostly straightforward.

sentences.zh: 皆務于農事，工習獵射，于書計非其長矣。

translations.literal: All devote themselves to farming; they are skilled in hunting and archery, but writing and reckoning are not their strength.
translations.idiomatic: All devote themselves to farming; they are skilled in hunting and archery, but writing and reckoning are not their strength.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡、臨邛、眉山、隆山、資陽、瀘川、巴東、遂甯、巴西、新城、金山、普安、犍為、越巂、䍧柯、黔安，得蜀之舊域。

translations.literal: Shu Commandery, Linqiong, Meishan, Longshan, Ziyang, Luchuan, Badong, Suining, Baxi, Xincheng, Jinshan, Pu'an, Qianwei, Yuexi, Zangke, and Qian'an comprise the old territory of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Commandery, Linqiong, Meishan, Longshan, Ziyang, Luchuan, Badong, Suining, Baxi, Xincheng, Jinshan, Pu'an, Qianwei, Yuexi, Zangke, and Qian'an comprise the old territory of Shu.

sentences.zh: 其地四塞，山川重阻，水陸所湊，貨殖所萃，蓋一都之會也。

translations.literal: Its land is enclosed on four sides, mountains and rivers form heavy barriers, water and land routes converge, and goods gather—it is truly the meeting place of a great capital.
translations.idiomatic: Its land is enclosed on four sides, mountains and rivers form heavy barriers, water and land routes converge, and goods gather—it is truly the meeting place of a great capital.

sentences.zh: 昔劉備資之，以成三分之業。

translations.literal: In former times Liu Bei relied on it to achieve the enterprise of the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Liu Bei relied on it to achieve the enterprise of the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 自金行喪亂，四海沸騰，李氏據之於前，譙氏依之於後。

translations.literal: Since the fall of the Jin metal line, the four seas boiled; the Li clan held it first, and the Qiao clan relied on it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Jin metal line, the four seas boiled; the Li clan held it first, and the Qiao clan relied on it afterward.

sentences.zh: 當梁氏將亡，武陵憑險而取敗，後周之末，王謙負固而速禍。

translations.literal: When the Liang house was near its end, the Prince of Wuling relied on its perilous terrain and met defeat; at the end of Later Zhou, Wang Qian relied on its defenses and quickly brought calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang house was near its end, the Prince of Wuling relied on its perilous terrain and met defeat; at the end of Later Zhou, Wang Qian relied on its defenses and quickly brought calamity.

sentences.zh: 故孟門不祀，古人所以誡焉。

translations.literal: Thus Meng Gate goes un-sacrificed—the ancients warned of this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Meng Gate goes un-sacrificed—the ancients warned of this.

sentences.zh: 其風俗大抵與漢中不別。

translations.literal: Its customs are largely no different from those of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs differ little from those of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 其人敏慧輕急，貌多蕞陋，頗慕文學，時有斐然，多溺于逸樂，少從宦之士，或至耆年白首，不離鄉邑。

translations.literal: Its people are quick-witted and impulsive, mostly short in stature, greatly fond of literature, and sometimes achieve brilliance; yet many drown in pleasure, and few follow official careers—even to old age with white hair, they do not leave their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Its people are quick-witted and impulsive, mostly short in stature, greatly fond of literature, and sometimes achieve brilliance; yet many drown in pleasure, and few follow official careers—even to old age with white hair, they do not leave their native districts.

sentences.zh: 人多工巧，綾錦雕鏤之妙，殆侔于上國。

translations.literal: The people are highly skilled in craftsmanship; the fineness of their brocades and carved inlay nearly rivals that of the central domains.
translations.idiomatic: The people are highly skilled in craftsmanship; the fineness of their brocades and carved inlay nearly rivals that of the central domains.

sentences.zh: 貧家不務儲蓄，富室專於趨利。

translations.literal: Poor families do not bother with savings; wealthy households devote themselves solely to chasing profit.
translations.idiomatic: Poor families do not bother with savings; wealthy households devote themselves solely to chasing profit.

sentences.zh: 其處家室，則女勤作業，而士多自閑，聚會宴飲，尤足意錢之戲。

translations.literal: In household affairs, women labor at production while men mostly idle themselves; at gatherings for feasting and drinking, they especially delight in gambling games.
translations.idiomatic: In household affairs, women labor at production while men mostly idle themselves; at gatherings for feasting and drinking, they especially delight in gambling games.

sentences.zh: 小人薄于情禮，父子率多異居。

translations.literal: Common people are lax in ritual and affection; fathers and sons mostly live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Common people are lax in ritual and affection; fathers and sons mostly live apart.

sentences.zh: 其邊野富人，多規固山澤，以財物雄役夷、獠，故輕為奸藏，權傾州縣。

translations.literal: Wealthy men on the frontier often seize mountains and marshes by force, using wealth to dominate the Yi and Liao peoples; thus they lightly engage in secret hoarding and their power overawes the provinces and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men on the frontier often seize mountains and marshes by force, using wealth to dominate the Yi and Liao peoples; thus they lightly engage in secret hoarding and their power overawes the provinces and counties.

translations.literal: Is this also their old custom?
translations.idiomatic: Is this also their old custom?

sentences.zh: 又有獽狿蠻賨，其居處風俗，衣服飲食，頗同於獠，而亦與蜀人相類。

translations.literal: There are also the Xian, Ran, Man, and Cong peoples; their dwellings, customs, clothing, and food are quite similar to the Liao, yet also resemble the people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: There are also the Xian, Ran, Man, and Cong peoples; their dwellings, customs, clothing, and food are quite similar to the Liao, yet also resemble the people of Shu.
